title: macOS Beta: Golden Gate Release Candidate now available
content:
Macworld





Following its preview at WWDC on June 8, Apple released the first developer beta of macOS 27 Golden Gate, giving developers and Mac users an early look at the next major version of macOS ahead of its expected public release later this month.
Rather than introducing a dramatic redesign, Golden Gate focuses on improving the experience established by macOS 26 Tahoe. The update brings Siri AI, deeper Apple Intelligence integration, smarter search tools, and a range of performance enhancements, while refining some of the more controversial aspects of Tahoe’s Liquid Glass interface.
As with any beta software, early access comes with risks. Bugs, app compatibility issues, and incomplete features are common, particularly in early developer releases. Before installing the macOS beta, it’s worth understanding what’s new, what issues testers are reporting, and whether it’s stable enough for your Mac.
Here’s everything you need to know about the latest macOS beta, including new features, known issues, release dates, and whether it’s worth installing.


What’s the latest macOS beta? 
Apple is currently running two macOS beta tracks for developers: the upcoming macOS 27 Golden Gate and updates for the current release, macOS 26 Tahoe.
Apple also runs a public beta, which allows enthusiasts and early adopters to test new features before the final version launches. You need to register for Apple’s public beta to access it.
macOS 27 Golden Gate beta version tracker 
Apple released the macOS 27 Golden Gate Public Beta 6 on August 31. 
Apple released macOS 27 Golden Gate Developer Release Candidate on September 9, 2026. 
Public Beta RC should be released sometime this week; new versions are usually released a day or two after the new developer beta.
macOS 26 Tahoe beta: Apple continues to develop macOS Tahoe through regular point releases.


						

							




macOS Beta timeline


ReleaseDate
Beta 1June 8, 2026
Beta 2June 22, 2026
Beta 3July 6, 2026
Beta 3 v.2July 13, 2026
Beta 4July 20, 2026
Beta 5August 10, 2026
Beta 6August 17, 2026
Beta 7August 24, 2026
Beta 8August 31, 2026
Release Candidate 1September 9, 2026
Public BetaJuly 13, 2026
Public Beta 2July 22, 2026
Public Beta 3August 11, 2026
Public Beta 4August 17, 2026
Public Beta 5August 24, 2026
Public Beta 6August 31, 2026
Final ReleaseSeptember

 






What’s new in the latest beta?

				
					

				
			
New features in macOS 27.

Foundry




The beta introduces several significant upgrades.
Siri AI: Apple has redesigned Siri with personal context awareness and the ability to perform multi-step tasks across apps.
Better performance: One of Golden Gate’s goals is improved responsiveness. Early testers report faster app launches, quicker AirDrop transfers, and a generally snappier experience than Tahoe.
Smarter Search: A rebuilt indexing engine powers Spotlight, Mail, and Photos, delivering faster and more relevant search results.
Safari Automation: Safari gains new AI-powered features, including automatic tab grouping and a new “Notify Me” tool that can monitor webpages for changes.
Design refinements: Following criticism of Tahoe’s Liquid Glass design, Apple has refined the interface with improved transparency controls and more consistent window corners.
More Apple Intelligence features: Apple Intelligence is integrated more deeply throughout the system. Improvements include smarter automation, enhanced password management, and natural-language shortcuts. Users can create Shortcuts using plain English, while Calendar can generate events from written requests. Photos also gains AI-powered editing tools, including Spatial Reframing and enhanced cleanup features.
Xcode 27: Xcode 27 ships with the macOS 27 SDK and includes new AI-assisted development tools, including coding assistance and testing features.
See Apple’s developer website for more information about the beta. 


						

							


Should you install the macOS beta?

				
					

				
			
Apple




While installing a beta lets you try new features such as Siri AI and enhanced Spotlight months before release, it is generally not recommended for most users because of the stability risks involved.
Install if…
You need to test apps
You want early access to new features
You have a secondary Mac available
Wait if…
This is your primary work machine
You rely on niche or specialist software
Stability is critical to your workflow


						

							






Who are you Should you install?

A developer testing appsInstall now
An Apple enthusiast with a spare MacConsider waiting for the Public Beta 
A public beta testers on main machineWait for the Public Beta
Mission-critical usersWait for fall 2026 version 

 






What do people think of the macOS beta?
Golden Gate is focused less on introducing dramatic new features and more on refining the experience introduced in macOS Tahoe. Early feedback has been positive about the ways Apple is addressing many of the complaints users had about 2025’s Liquid Glass redesign while also improving overall performance.
Performance: Reports from beta testers both within our team and across the web suggest that Golden Gate feels faster and more responsive. Some users report that even older Macs feel noticeably quicker when running the beta.
Liquid Glass changes: Early testers appear supportive of the updated design. Apple has refined several Liquid Glass elements and introduced greater control over transparency effects.
Siri AI: The biggest addition in Golden Gate is Siri AI. However, support outside Apple’s own apps remains inconsistent. Some testers find Siri AI genuinely useful, while others report reliability issues.
Read: macOS Golden Gate vs macOS Tahoe: What’s new and should you upgrade?


						

							


What are the risks of installing beta software?
Installing pre-release software on a primary device carries several risks.
System instability: Performance problems, freezes, crashes, and other unexpected behavior are common during beta testing.
App failures: Third-party applications may crash, behave unpredictably, or stop working entirely.
Hardware strain: Early beta builds can increase battery drain and cause Macs to run hotter than usual.
Data loss: Software bugs may corrupt files, and downgrading to a stable version often requires a complete system reset.


						

							


Safety precautions and best practices
If you decide to install the beta, take the following precautions:
Use a secondary device: Avoid installing beta software on your primary Mac or on any machine used for critical work.
Create a full backup: Use Time Machine to create a complete backup before upgrading so you can restore your Mac if something goes wrong. Note that this need to be a Time Machine backup from before the beta was installed and you will lose anything saved subsequently. 
Install on a separate volume: Consider installing the beta on a separate volume or external SSD rather than replacing your main operating system.
Check storage space: Make sure you have at least 15GB of free storage available before beginning the installation.


						

							


How to install the macOS beta

				
					

				
			
Foundry




The process for installing a macOS beta depends on whether you are seeking the Developer Beta or the Public Beta. Apple simplified this process a few years ago, removing the need for a paid developer account to access early builds. 
The first step is to join Apple’s beta testing program. We explain how to do that in a separate article.
You will need to register your account either as a public beta tester or as a developer in order to enable beta updates on your Mac.
To install the beta follow these steps:
Back up your Mac: Before installing any pre-release software, it is critical to prepare your Mac to avoid data loss. Beta software is inherently unstable and can cause crashes or app compatibility issues. 
Registered your account either as a public beta tester or as a developer in order to enable beta updates on your Mac:
For the Public Beta: Visit the Apple Beta Software Program website, sign in with your Apple ID, and agree to the terms.
For the Developer Beta: Register as an Apple Developer on Apple’s website, download the Apple Developer app from the App Store, sign in with your standard Apple ID, and complete the free registration process.
On the Mac where you wish to install the beta, open System Settings and navigate to General > Software Update.
Click the (i) info button next to Beta Updates.
Enable Beta Updates.
The beta will appear as an available upgrade. Select the macOS beta you want to instal (e.g., macOS 27 Golden Gate Public Beta or Developer Beta).
Click Upgrade Now to begin the download and installation.
As long as you are a registered developer or enrolled in the public beta program, when the relevant macOS Beta becomes available, it will also show up on your Mac.
Once you are running the beta, the updates will come through to your Mac automatically; you just need to go to Software Update in System Settings and click to install. See How to install macOS.


						

							


How to get a free Apple developer account
If you just want a free Apple Developer account so you can access the beta, you can get this via Xcode or the Apple Developer app in iOS. Here’s how to do it via the Apple Developer app on an iPhone:
Get the Apple Developer App from the App Store. 
Open the app on your iPhone. 
Tap on Account. 
Tap on Sign In. 
Sign in using your usual Apple ID. 
If you wish to actually publish applications to the App Store or receive support, you’ll need to pay $99/£79 per year for a paid account. You can compare the free and paid accounts here.


						

							





 FAQ 


1.
Who can run the macOS beta?
Anyone can run the macOS beta, but to do so, you do need to register for either the developer beta, the pubic beta, or both.
Apple offers both developer and public beta programs for macOS, enabling all interested users to test pre-release versions of the operating system. While both betas provide early access to new features, they cater to different user profiles based on technical expertise and risk tolerance. Beta software tends to be buggy so the more stable public beta version may be preferable, but even that will not be bug-free.
In the past, the developer beta was only available to developers who had paid to join Apple’s Developer Program (which costs $99/£79). However, for a couple of years now, Apple has opened up the developer beta to registered developers with free developer accounts. We explain how to get a free developer account below. 
If you decide you no longer want to run the beta version of macOS read this: How to remove the macOS beta.





2.
macOS public beta vs developer beta
Since 2023, the Developer Beta has been available to anyone who registers as a developer, even if they aren’t a paid-up member of Apple’s Developer Program. As a result, people with a basic free developer account can download the new macOS developer beta (we show you how to register below).
Whether you should download the developer beta if you aren’t a developer is another question. We don’t recommend you install the developer beta if you aren’t a developer. Instead, our recommendation is to use the public beta (the first version of which usually arrives in July).
There are a few differences between the public and developer betas. The public beta is not the same as the beta that is released through the developer program. The public beta typically launches after the developer beta has undergone initial testing and refinement
Developers get updates to their beta first, and possibly more frequently. But you should keep in mind that betas are by nature not stable, and because the public beta comes after the developer beta it could be a little safer to install. 
The most significant difference is probably the motive of the testers: Developers usually have the aim of ensuring their apps work when the updated macOS is released to the general public, while public beta testers are essentially helping Apple detect bugs and offering feedback on the features. Because of this, developers may get to test new features not available in the public beta. 
If you want to get the public beta the first thing you need to do, if you haven’t already, is join Apple’s beta programs read this for more information: How to become an Apple beta tester.





3.
Is the macOS beta stable?
By its nature, a beta has the potential to be unstable. Therefore, it’s not advised that you install it on a Mac that you rely on. If you have a second Mac that isn’t mission-critical, then install it there. We strongly recommend that you don’t risk all by putting the macOS beta on your primary macOS, especially not in the early days of the beta development. 
If you don’t have a second Mac, there are a couple of ways you could run macOS beta on your Mac without running the risk of losing data or finding your Mac stops working:
We recommend installing it on a partition, which these days is really a volume (and is much easier to create than a partition was). Read about how to do that here: How to dual-boot Mac: Run two versions of macOS on a Mac.
Alternatively, you could install the macOS beta on an external drive and run it on that.
We discuss the safety of the macOS beta and the risks you might be taking in more detail in a separate article.
If the stability of the beta worries you, then you are probably better off waiting until the final version is out, or at least waiting until testing has been happening for a few months before getting the beta.





4.
How to prepare your Mac for the beta
Update your software: We recommend you have the latest full version of macOS installed, although Apple says that the macOS Developer Beta Access Utility requires macOS 10.8 or later.
Make space: We’d recommend at least 15GB of available space because the macOS betas tend to be very large. If you end up requiring more space, read: How to free up space on Mac. Note that we always recommend that you have at least 10% space free on your Mac at any time, so if you don’t have that, expect problems!
Back up: Before you install a beta on your Mac, you should make a backup of your data and files. You can find out how to use Time Machine to back up your Mac. We also have a round-up of suitable backup solutions.





5.
How to send feedback to Apple
Should you come across an error or a bug, you should use the Feedback Assistant app to provide feedback to Apple. Launch the app and follow the appropriate steps, selecting the area about which you’re providing feedback and then any specific sub-area. Then describe your issue in a single sentence, before providing a more detailed description, including any specific steps that reproduce the issue. You’ll also be able to attach other files.
You’ll also have to give permission for the Feedback Assistant app to collect diagnostic information from your Mac.
It won’t always be obvious whether something is a bug or just not as easy to use as you might have hoped. Either way, if your feedback is that something appears to work in an illogical way, Apple will want to know that.
If you are having trouble with a third-party app, you can let Apple know by reporting it through the 3rd-party Application Compatibility category in the Feedback Assistant. However, we’d suggest that you also provide feedback to the app’s developer, who will no doubt be grateful.





6.
Will I be able to update from macOS beta to the final version?
Beta users will be able to install the final build of the OS on release day without needing to reformat or reinstall.





7.
Can I talk about the beta publicly?
According to Apple and the license agreement all beta testers must agree to, the beta is “Apple confidential information”. By accepting those terms, you agree not to discuss your use of the software with anyone who isn’t also in the Beta Software Program. That means you can’t “blog, post screenshots, tweet, or publicly post information about the public beta software.”
However, you can discuss any information that Apple has publicly disclosed; the company says that information is no longer considered confidential.





8.
How to downgrade from the macOS beta
You can always revert to an earlier version of macOS, though depending on how you back up, it’s not necessarily a painless process.
Start by making sure the data on your drive is backed up, then erase the drive and install the latest public version of macOS. When you first start up your Mac, you can use the Migration Assistant to import your data from the backup. Here’s a more detailed tutorial on downgrading from the macOS beta and we also have a tutorial on downgrading to an older version of the Mac OS.





9.
Is the beta free to download? 
Yes, the macOS beta is free to download for both developers and the general public. Apple offers two distinct tracks for testing pre-release software: the Developer Beta and the Public Beta, both of which are now accessible without a paid subscription.





10.
Can I go back to the stable version?
Yes, you can go back to the stable version of macOS from a beta, but the complexity of the process depends on whether the final version of that software has been released yet.
If you are running a beta (such as the macOS 27 Golden Gate beta) and want to return to the current stable version (such as macOS 26 Tahoe) before the new OS officially launches in the fall, you must perform a clean installation. Because this requires wiping your internal drive, a full backup is essential, but you will want a backup made before you installed the macOS beta.





11.
Should I install the beta on my main Mac?
Installing a macOS beta on your primary computer is generally not recommended due to the inherent risks of using unfinished software. While beta programs offer early access to new features, they are designed for testing and often contain significant bugs that can disrupt your daily workflow.





12.
Do I need an Apple Developer account to install the beta?
You do not need a paid Apple Developer account to install the macOS beta. While access to developer betas was previously restricted to those paying a $99/£79 annual fee, Apple changed this policy in 2023 to allow anyone with a free developer account to access these builds . Alternatively, you can join the Public Beta program, which is also free and accessible to anyone with a valid Apple ID.





13.
How often are new beta versions released?
New macOS beta versions are typically released every one to two weeks, with the frequency increasing as the final public release date approaches. The beta updates refine features and address bugs identified by testers.





14.
Is the macOS beta safe to install?
The beta is generally safe to test, but it may contain bugs that cause crashes, poor battery life, app compatibility issues, or data loss. Always back up your Mac before installing.





15.
Will my apps work with the macOS beta?
Many apps will work normally, but some third-party software may crash, perform poorly, or not launch at all until developers release updates.

title: Apple Watch Series 12 & Ultra 4: Everything you need to know about the new Apple Watches
content:
Macworld





Apple has unveiled the Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4, with both models focusing much more heavily on health monitoring, Apple Intelligence and battery efficiency than on physical redesigns. Series 12 remains Apple’s mainstream premium smartwatch, while Ultra 4 continues as the larger, tougher model aimed at endurance sports, outdoor activities and diving. Both are available to pre-order now and go on sale on September 18.
The biggest upgrade shared by both watches is Apple’s all-new Health Sensing System, which combines redesigned optical and electrical heart sensors with larger, more power-efficient green LEDs. Apple says it provides the most accurate heart-rate sensing of any wearable it tested. Background heart-rate readings are now taken every five seconds, while HRV can be measured as often as every five minutes – 60 times and 24 times more frequently respectively than on Series 11.
That additional data powers another major addition: Readiness, which gives users a 0–10 score based on recent activity, sleep, vitals and recovery data, and updates during the day. Both watches also use Apple’s new S11 chip, which enables Siri AI and a collection of Audio Intelligence features including Sound Recognition, faster Shazam, Live Rewind and Siri Recap. Some of those Audio Intelligence features won’t arrive until later in 2026.
The most dramatic hardware improvement is reserved for the Ultra 4: Apple has increased normal battery life from 42 hours to 50 hours, Low Power Mode from 72 to 84 hours, and introduced workout modes capable of tracking for up to 45 hours. Series 12 remains rated at 24 hours, although its quick charging is more useful, while the aluminium Series 12 gains tougher Ceramic Shield 2 and Apple has brought back a premium ceramic Apple Watch for the first time in years.
The five biggest Apple Watch upgrades for 2026
New Health Sensing System with substantially more frequent heart-rate and HRV monitoring.
Readiness score for daily recovery and training guidance.
S11 chip, Siri AI and Audio Intelligence, including Siri Recap and Live Rewind.
Much longer Ultra 4 battery life, rising from 42 to 50 hours, with up to 45 hours of extended workout tracking.
New materials and durability, including Ceramic Shield 2 on aluminium Series 12 and the return of ceramic Series 12 models.
The rumours were broadly right that this wouldn’t be a major redesign, and also correctly predicted the emphasis on health, Siri AI and ceramic materials. However, rumours of Touch ID have not materialised, there is still no blood-glucose sensor, and the Series 12 hasn’t gained longer quoted battery life despite speculation about a larger battery. Apple also resisted the predicted price increase.

				
					

				
			
Your watch knows how you are feeling. Do you? 

Apple




Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4: Top 10 features


FeatureApple Watch Series 12Apple Watch Ultra 4

Health Sensing SystemNew optical/electrical sensorsSame new system
Background heart rateEvery 5 secondsEvery 5 seconds
HRVAs often as every 5 minutesAs often as every 5 minutes
Readiness scoreYesYes, with training data
ProcessorS11S11
Siri AIYesYes
Audio IntelligenceYesYes
Display42mm/46mm, up to 2,000 nits49mm, up to 3,000 nits
BatteryUp to 24 hours; 38 hours Low PowerUp to 50 hours; 84 hours Low Power
SatelliteNo direct satellite communicationsEmergency SOS and Find My via satellite

 






Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 release date: When will they go on sale?
Apple announced the Series 12 and Ultra 4 on September 9, 2026.
Both watches are available to pre-order immediately, including in the U.S., U.K., Australia, Canada and more than 50 other countries and regions.
They officially go on sale and become available in Apple Stores on Friday, September 18, 2026.
You can buy them directly from Apple through Apple.com, the Apple Store app and Apple retail stores. They will also be available through Apple-authorised retailers and, in the case of cellular models, participating mobile networks.
watchOS 27 arrives slightly earlier, on September 14, for compatible existing Apple Watches.
Pre-order Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 at Apple U.S. 
Pre-order Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 at Apple U.K. 


							


Apple Watch Series 12 design

				
					

				
			
The Apple Watch Series 12 in bronze.

Apple




The Series 12 does not represent a major external redesign, as the pre-launch rumours suggested. It retains Apple’s familiar rounded-square design and comes in 42mm and 46mm sizes.
Interestingly, the aluminium and titanium cases are fractionally wider than Series 11. The 46mm model measures 46 x 40 x 9.7mm, compared with 46 x 39 x 9.7mm for Series 11. The 42mm version measures 42 x 37 x 9.7mm, compared with 42 x 36 x 9.7mm previously. The screen resolutions remain 416×496 pixels and 374×446 pixels respectively.
Apple continues to offer aluminium and titanium models, but ceramic has returned as a premium case option. Ceramic models are fractionally larger and thicker, measuring 43mm or 47mm tall and 9.85mm thick.
The finishes are:
Aluminium: Dark Bronze, Light Gold, Black and Space Grey
Titanium: Radiant Gold and Natural
Ceramic: Pearl White and Night Blue
The ceramic options confirm one of the more interesting pre-launch rumours, although Apple opted for Night Blue rather than the dark grey that had also been indicated.
The Series 12 display remains a wide-angle LTPO3 Always-On Retina OLED with up to 2,000 nits brightness. Aluminium models now use Ceramic Shield 2, which Apple says is 60 percent tougher than the Ion-X glass used on Series 11. Titanium and ceramic versions use sapphire crystal.


						

							


Apple Watch Ultra 4 design

				
					

				
			
The rugged Apple Watch Ultra 4.

Apple




The Ultra 4 changes even less externally. It remains a 49mm Grade 5 titanium watch, measuring exactly 49 x 44 x 12mm, with the same 422×514-pixel display and 1,245 sq mm display area as Ultra 3.
It comes in the familiar Natural Titanium and Black Titanium finishes and retains its flat sapphire crystal display, raised protective case edges, prominent Digital Crown and orange-accented Action button.
The Ultra 4 is slightly heavier, however: 63.0g in Natural and 63.1g in Black, compared with 61.6g and 61.8g respectively for Ultra 3.
The display remains a wide-angle LTPO3 Always-On Retina display capable of 3,000 nits, so there is no headline screen-brightness upgrade.
Apple hasn’t introduced the rumoured Touch ID fingerprint sensor on the 2026 Apple Watch models. 


						

							


What about the buttons and controls?

				
					

				
			
The side button.

Apple




The physical control layout is essentially unchanged.
Series 12 has:
Digital Crown with haptic feedback
Side button
Strap-release buttons
Ultra 4 adds the familiar:
Customisable Action button
Larger protected Digital Crown
Side button
The Action button can start workouts, mark segments, move to the next interval, activate the torch and perform other user-selected actions.
There is, however, a new single-tap finger-and-thumb gesture in addition to Double Tap and Wrist Flick, providing another way to interact without touching the display.


						

							


Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 processor: What processor do they use?
Both watches use Apple’s new S11 chip, replacing the S10 used by Series 11 and Ultra 3.
Apple’s specifications list:
64-bit dual-core processor
4-core Neural Engine
64GB storage
Secure hardware for Audio Intelligence processing
The S10 also had a 64-bit dual-core CPU, four-core Neural Engine and 64GB of storage, so the headline specifications alone don’t reveal how much faster S11 actually is. Apple calls it its “most powerful wearable chip”, but notably hasn’t provided a percentage CPU or GPU performance improvement over S10, and its technical specifications don’t list a separate GPU core count.
That means the more important S11 improvements appear to be what the chip enables rather than raw benchmark performance.
It works with the new Health Sensing System, supports Siri AI and powers the new Audio Intelligence functionality. Apple has also emphasised efficiency, particularly in relation to higher-frequency sensor readings and Ultra 4’s improved battery life.
The new Audio Intelligence system includes a Secure Exclave, a hardware-isolated area of the S11 that processes audio separately and deletes raw audio immediately after processing.


						

							


2026 Apple Watch connectivity
Connectivity changes are modest. Cellular Series 12 and Ultra 4 models support 5G RedCap and LTE, as did their predecessors, with no newly branded Apple-designed modem.
Both watches also support Wi-Fi 4 (802.11n) on 2.4GHz and 5GHz, Bluetooth 5.3, and Apple’s second-generation Ultra Wideband chip. Wi-Fi 4 may sound dated, but Apple Watch relies mainly on Bluetooth and has relatively low data requirements.
Satellite connectivity
Satellite communications remain a major distinction between the Series and Ultra families.
Apple Watch Series 12 doesn’t have built-in satellite connectivity.
Ultra 4 does, supporting Emergency SOS via satellite and Find My location sharing via satellite when cellular and Wi-Fi aren’t available.
This is broadly what had been expected before launch: satellite remains primarily an Ultra feature rather than migrating to the regular Series watch.


						

							


2026 Apple Watch battery and charging: What’s new?

				
					

				
			
Charging the Apple Watch. 

Apple




Apple Watch Series 12
Apple rates Series 12 for:
Up to 24 hours normal use
Up to 38 hours in Low Power Mode
Up to 10 hours of outdoor workout tracking
Those first two figures are unchanged from Series 11, so despite rumours that Apple was working on a larger battery, there is no increase in Apple’s quoted everyday battery life.
Charging has improved, however.
Series 12 can reach:
80 percent in around 30 minutes
Up to 12 hours of use from a 15-minute charge
Up to 10 hours of sleep tracking from five minutes of charging
Series 11 also reached 80 percent in around 30 minutes, but a 15-minute charge provided only around eight hours of normal use.
Apple Watch Ultra 4
Battery life is one of Ultra 4’s biggest upgrades.
Apple rates it for:
50 hours normal use, up from 42 hours
84 hours Low Power Mode, up from 72 hours
18 hours standard outdoor workout tracking
25 hours Extended Workout
45 hours Max Extended Workout
Apple says the Extended Workout figure represents a 25 percent increase over the previous generation.
Charging remains capable of reaching 80 percent in around 45 minutes, but 15 minutes of charging now provides up to 18 hours of use, versus 12 hours on Ultra 3.
Apple also credits more efficient workout algorithms with helping deliver the longer endurance.
Apple Watch charging
Both models use Apple’s magnetic fast-charging system with the Apple Watch Magnetic Fast Charger to USB-C Cable.
There is no conventional wired charging port on either watch and no change to the basic magnetic charging system this year.


						

							




Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 price
Apple has kept its entry prices unchanged in both the U.S. and U.K. – contrary to pre-event speculation that the Series 12 could increase in price.


Model2026 pricePrevious generation

Series 12 – U.S.From $399Series 11: $399
Series 12 – U.K.From £369Series 11: £369
Ultra 4 – U.S.From $799Ultra 3: $799
Ultra 4 – U.K.From £749Ultra 3: £749

 



Series 12 pricing varies considerably depending on case material. Aluminium is the entry-level option, while titanium costs more and the newly revived ceramic models occupy the premium end of the range.
The fact that Apple hasn’t increased the base prices is significant because our pre-launch assessment suggested a Series 12 increase to around $429 was possible. That prediction hasn’t materialised.
Should you buy Apple Watch Series 12 or Ultra 4?

				
					

				
			
Apple




Apple Watch Series 12 is the best choice for most people. It offers essentially all of Apple’s important new health features – including the new Health Sensing System, Readiness, frequent HRV measurements, Siri AI and Audio Intelligence – in a considerably smaller and cheaper watch.
The strongest reason to choose Ultra 4 is battery life. Its jump from 42 to 50 hours makes it much more practical for people who regularly spend more than a day away from a charger, while the new 25- and 45-hour extended workout modes make it substantially more appealing to runners, hikers, cyclists and endurance athletes.
Ultra 4 is also the better choice for outdoor adventurers because of its brighter 3,000-nit display, dual-frequency GPS, rugged titanium construction, Action button, 100m water resistance, recreational diving support and satellite communications. Series 12 is the better everyday watch: lighter, less bulky, available in two sizes and substantially cheaper.

title: Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 Offer These Eight New Health and Fitness Features
content:
The Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 offer a range of new health and fitness features. Here's everything that's new.


Apple today revealed the following features for the two new devices:


New "Health Sensing System": A redesigned sensor architecture with three main improvements, including increased electrode surface area for better ECG skin contact, photodiodes arranged in a ring for more efficient light capture, and larger, more power-efficient green LEDs for accurate heart rate readings during motion.

Continuous heart rate sensing: Heart rate is now measured every five seconds throughout the day, 60 times more frequently than before, viewable via a new watch face complication.

Higher-frequency HRV: Heart rate variability is sampled up to 24 times more often, with separate recovery and overall HRV values shown in a new section of the Heart Rate app.

Daytime vitals view: A new toggle lets users switch between overnight and daytime vitals, potentially catching shifts in metrics before they show up in overnight readings.

VO2 Max test: A new test has users set up their iPhone to watch them perform a series of exercises, delivering results immediately alongside data from their Apple Watch.

Most accurate step tracking: A redesigned pedometer model with new machine learning algorithms improves distance accuracy for indoor workouts and all-day step counts.

Steps complication: A brand-new watch face complication, enabled by the S11 chip, lets users track their step count in real time.

Longer workout battery life: Up to 10 hours during an outdoor workout, 25% more than the previous model, with 15 minutes of charging now delivering up to 12 hours of extra battery. The Apple Watch Ultra 4 goes further, with up to 50 hours of everyday battery life, 84 hours in Low Power Mode, and a new Max Extended Workout mode rated for up to 45 hours of outdoor tracking; 15 minutes of charging adds up to 18 hours of battery.

title: Apple Reveals iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max Battery Capacities
content:
Apple has confirmed the battery capacities for the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max models that the company announced earlier today.


Apple is required to publish energy labels on its iPhone product pages in the EU, and they reveal the official mAh battery capacities for the devices.

Here are the battery capacities for the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max models that still have a SIM card tray, according to Apple:


  
iPhone 18 Pro: 4,056 mAh (+1.7% vs. iPhone 17 Pro's 3,988 mAh)

  
iPhone 18 Pro Max: 5,391 mAh (+11.7% vs. iPhone 17 Pro Max's 4,823 mAh)

Notably, the iPhone 18 Pro Max has received a much larger battery life increase than the iPhone 18 Pro did compared to the previous generation.

eSIM-only models of the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max will be available in Bahrain, Canada, Guam, Japan, Kuwait, Mexico, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, the U.S., and the U.S. Virgin Islands. The devices have a SIM card tray in all other countries around the world, including in the U.K. and the rest of Europe.

eSIM-only iPhone models are equipped with a slightly larger battery that fills the space occupied by the physical SIM card tray.

title: Everything Apple announced at its Surprise and Shine event
content:
Macworld





Apple’s “Surprise and Shine” event might be the most anticipated iPhone keynote in 10 years. It all kicks off today, and like you, we can’t wait! So join us as we count down the hours and minutes with all the latest rumors, leaks, and speculation leading up to the big event on Wednesday, September 9, at 10 am PT.
Surprise and Shine iPhone event: How to watch
You can watch the full keynote right here using the embedded YouTube link below or on Apple.com on your iPhone or Mac. The “Watch Now” tab in the TV app on the Apple TV will also show the stream live.






Surprise and Shine Apple event: Everything announced
Apple has wrapped up its September Surprise and Shine event, and while there weren’t a ton of surprises, we did get a lot of new Apple products. Here’s everything Apple announced today:
iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max
Apple’s newest flagship iPhones look the same as last year’s models but have some notable new features. The main one is a variable aperture on the main 48MP wide-angle camera. It will dynamically adjust how much light the lens lets in to take better pictures in low light and bright light, while capturing better detail.
The phones come in four new colors: Burgandy, Glacier (Light Blue), Silver, and Black. They start at higher prices than last year: $1,199 for the Pro and $1,299 for the Pro Max with 256GB of storage. Prices go up quite a bit more for higher storage tiers, with the 2TB iPhone 18 Pro Max costing a whopping $2,499. Pre-orders begin Saturday and will ship next Friday, September 18.
Read more about the new phones here.

				
					

				
			
Apple




AirPods 5
The latest AirPods still start at $129, but that’s with active noise cancellation, so effectively a $50 price cut over the AirPods 4. They look similar to the AirPods 4, but Apple says AirPods 5 remove up to 50 percent more noise compared to AirPods 4 with ANC thanks to a new multiport acoustic architecture and improved computational audio algorithms.
For an extra $20, you can get a wireless charging case and AirPods Pro-like stem volume controls. Both models are available for preorder today and will ship September 18.
Read more about the new AirPods here.
Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4
The Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 also look the same as last year’s models, but they have significant change inside. The watches feature a new Health Sensing System, which uses the S11 chip and new optical and electrical heart sensors to deliver deeper insight into a user’s fitness and physiological state while making Exercise and Move Activity rings even more accurate.
There’s also a new Readiness app that analyzes a user’s recent activity, training load, vitals, and sleep score to offer insight into their capacity for the day ahead as well as longer battery life and a redesigned Health app. They also get new Apple Intelligence features, including Siri Recap, which creates high-level summaries of conversations throughout the day, and Live Rewind, which can show you the previous 15 seconds of a conversation so you don’t need to ask someone to repeat themselves.
The watches start at the same prices as before ($399 for the 42mm Series 12 and $799 for the Ultra 4), but the larger 46mm Series 12 is a little higher, starting at $449 (previously $429).
Read more about the new watches here.

				
					

				
			
Geräuscherkennung direkt auf der Apple Watch

Halyna Kubiv




iPhone Duo
Apple’s first folding phone is here and it’s better than any of the rumors you might have read. It has a 5.4-inch outer display that opens to a 7.6-inch inner display with the same ratio inside and out so apps seamlessly flow in and out. You can use it in a variety of ways, including as an alarm clock in Standby mode or a mini laptop with a virtual keyboard on the lower half when folded.
It has an A20 processor, C2 model, and dual 48MP camera system, as well as a 12MP FaceTime camera that’s entirely under the display for the first time ever on an iPhone. However, it doesn’t have Face ID, opting instead for Touch ID built into the power button.
 When opened, iPhone Duo is just 5.2mm thick and 11.3mm thick when folded. It has an IP68 dust resistance thanks to its hinge, which is engineered from more than 100 components to precisely control opening and closing and support the center of the display. There’s also a nano-textured cover layer on the inner display to minimize wear and creasing.
The iPhone Duo starts at $1,999 and will be available for pre-order on October 16 with shipping beginning October 23.
Read more about Apple’s new folding phone here.

title: Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4: Their 7 biggest surprises
content:
Macworld





At the Surprise and Shine press event today, Apple announced a raft of new products including the iPhone 18 Pro, AirPods 5, and iPhone Duo… and thanks to pre-launch rumors, surprises were in short supply. Nearly everything was leaked accurately ahead of time.
But one product that did manage to spring a few small surprises was the Apple Watch Series 12. Ahead of launch, we were led to expect a tedious iterative update with a new processor, identical design, and maybe a few new health features. Some of that was true, but there were unexpected pleasures as well.
Here are the 7 things we like best about the new Apple Watch Series 12 and its Apple Watch Ultra 4 sibling, which launched at the same time.
1. Stunning new materials
Granted, the design hasn’t changed in any fundamental way this year. (As I said on the live blog, the average member of the public would probably struggle to spot the difference between the Series 12 and the Series 4.) The leakers were right about that. But cosmetics matter too, and in that department Apple has done outstanding work with its watches this year.
Firstly, Apple has refreshed the color finishes. On the aluminum models, Silver and Rose Gold are gone, replaced by Light Gold (nice) and Dark Bronze (my favorite Apple Watch color so far). On the titanium side, Gold has been replaced by Radiant Gold, a definite improvement.
But the real aesthetic killer is the return of ceramic as a chassis material. The ceramic version of Series 12 comes in Night Blue and Pearl White, and they’re both gorgeous. You may think us shallow, but we’re pumped for the look of this year’s new watches. And watches, after all, are at least partly fashion items, so it’s okay to care about things like that.

				
					

				
			The stunning ceramic color options for the Apple Watch Series 12.
Apple




2. Tougher screens
The Series 11 had a tough screen… if you went for the more expensive titanium version. But as of the launch of the Series 12, Ceramic Shield 2 is on the aluminum models too, bringing (Apple claims) a 60 percent jump in durability compared to the mere Ion-X protective tech on the baseline Series 11. This brings an important feature within reach of less wealthy customers.
3. More accurate, all-day heart-rate sensing
This is one improvement we did know about ahead of the launch. What was surprising was the extent of Apple’s claims for the new devices.
The Apple Watch Series 12, according to Apple’s internal testing, has “the most accurate heart rate sensing in a wearable.” And that’s all down to a new sensor setup, combined with the powerful S11 processor.
The redesigned (sorry, “re-architected”) sensors ensure better skin contact during ECG readings, Apple says. There are redesigned photodiodes and larger, power-efficient green LEDs. All of this enables the Series 12 and Ultra 4 to measure your heart rate every five seconds, all day long, to a high degree of accuracy, helping the device to produce better insights about fitness, stress, and overall health.

				
					

				
			We’re excited about the updated heart-rate sensor. And also that bronze finish.
Apple




4. Health software that’s sophisticated but simple
Apple spent a lot of the presentation talking about software features, which is odd for a hardware event. One would imagine that most of these are part of watchOS 27, which was demoed and released in beta as long ago as June. Are the new features available on existing watches, provided they can run watchOS 27? Apple didn’t rush to make that clear in the keynote or its website, and it’s not hard to see why. Much better for customers to associate the features with the new hardware and pay for an upgrade.
But I digress. What was exciting about the keynote was seeing how much work Apple has done to improve and expand the health software on the Apple Watch. For example, there’s an entirely new app called Readiness, which “analyzes a user’s recent activity, training load, vitals, and sleep score to offer insight into their capacity for the day ahead.” What’s really nice is that it translates this complex analysis into a simple score out of 10 and a clear recommendation.
What may capture more users’ imagination is the new Longevity tab in Health, which includes Health Age: again, a simple way of communicating a complex set of factors. The Heart Rate app, meanwhile, gets a new section for tracking HRV, “a key indicator of stress and recovery,” which was already tracked but is measured much more often on the new watches. This is typical of the expanded array of health data analysis you can enjoy on the Series 12 and Ultra 4. And, possibly, your existing watch.
5. Cool AI audio features
Again, Apple didn’t go so far as to specify that the new AI/audio features grouped under the umbrella term Audio Intelligence are only for the Series 12 and Ultra 4. But it strongly implied and later confirmed that they’re made possible by the power of the S11 processor (described as Apple’s “most powerful wearable chip yet”).
What is clear is that these features have the potential to be very exciting. Sound Recognition alerts deaf and hard-of-hearing users about important sounds such as alarms and babies crying. Live Rewind, accessed via a double-press of the Digital Crown, displays the last 15 seconds of a conversation as text on your watch screen–perfect when you miss something important. And Siri Recap creates summaries of conversations. That last one is maybe a bit creepy (though it’s all private and stored on the device), but it’s still an impressive concept.

				
					

				
			
The new Siri Modular face could become a favorite thanks to the Apple Watch Series 12’s new AI features.

Apple




6. Longer battery life
Here’s an area where we weren’t expecting anything after last year’s unprecedented battery breakthrough. And sure enough, the baseline estimated battery life of the standard model remains at 24 hours. But the fact that battery life for outdoor workouts has gone up by 25 percent, now estimated at 10 hours, is a nice and unexpected bonus.
And now look at the Ultra 4. Last year, estimated general battery life went up from 36 hours to 42 hours. But this year it gets an even bigger increase, from 42 to 50 hours. There’s a new Extended Workout mode promising up to 25 hours of usage, even when tracking workouts with full GPS and heart rate readings. And for extreme situations, there’s Max Extended Workout mode, which can track outdoor runs and walks for up to 45 hours.
All that, and charging for both models is faster too. What a nice surprise.
7. No starting price hike
Arguably the biggest and nicest surprise of all: the starting price for the Series 12 and Ultra 4 are exactly the same as for the Series 11 and Ultra 3: $399 and $799. With RAM prices being the way they are, this was not something we saw coming. And the ceramic models, which previously started at over $1,249, now cost a much more palatable $899.
It’s not all good news in this area: certain upgraded models, such as the 46mm version of the Series 12, have gone up, albeit by small margins. But having the same baseline entry point is a major surprise.

title: iPhone 18 Pro Max Is Heavier Than iPhone 17 Pro Max, Not Thicker
content:
Despite rumors of an increase in thickness, the iPhone 18 Pro Max has the same physical dimensions as the iPhone 17 Pro Max. It is 163.4mm x 78mm x 8.75mm, but it did get 16 grams heavier.


Apple says the ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ Max weighs 249 grams, while the ‌iPhone 17 Pro‌ Max weighed 233 grams, making it the heaviest non-folding iPhone to date. It is heavier than the iPhone 14 Pro Max, which was previously Apple's weightiest iPhone at 240 grams.

The ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ weighs 211 grams, up from 206 grams in the prior-generation model. Apple may have increased battery size even though dimensions didn't change, or the new vapor chamber cooling system may be heavier heavier.

There's a bigger vapor chamber in the ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ models that takes up three times more surface area to dissipate more heat. The A20 Pro is able to deliver up to 40 percent better sustained performance than the A19 Pro thanks to the next-generation vapor chamber and "more thermally conductive materials."

The 18 Pro Max battery offers up to six hours more video playback than the battery in the ‌iPhone 17 Pro‌ Max.

iPhone Duo, which weighs 254 grams. The ‌iPhone Duo‌ is Apple's heaviest iPhone to date.

title: Apple Adds AppleCare One Family Plan for Up to Six People
content:
Apple today announced AppleCare One Family, a new option for U.S. customers that extends ‌AppleCare‌ coverage to every eligible device across an Apple Family Sharing group of up to six people for one fixed monthly price.


‌AppleCare‌ One Family costs $49.99 per month and includes all of the same benefits as ‌AppleCare‌+, such as coverage for accidental damage like drops and spills, battery replacement service, and priority support from Apple Experts. It also includes theft and loss protection for eligible iPhone, iPad, and Apple Watch models, and allows six total claims per year across the group.

Once a subscriber signs up, they can add devices from their iPhone, ‌iPad‌, or Mac, including "most devices less than four years old and in good working condition." Newly purchased devices are added automatically at no extra cost, and the price stays the same regardless of how many eligible products end up being covered.

To use the new plan, customers must set up Family Sharing in the Settings app on their iPhone, ‌iPad‌, or Mac and invite up to five other people to join. Any eligible devices those family members already own can then be covered under the same subscription, eliminating the need to buy and manage a separate ‌AppleCare‌ plan for each person.

AppleCare One, the multi-device subscription Apple introduced in the U.S. in July 2025 at $19.99 per month for up to three products. That plan has since expanded to Australia, France, Germany, and the UK, and today's announcement gives U.S. customers with larger households a way to consolidate coverage under a single subscription rather than juggling individual plans.

title: iPhone 18 Pro's $100 Price Increase is Actually $300 If You Want 1TB Storage
content:
Apple raised the base price of the iPhone 18 Pro and ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ Max by $100 compared to the iPhone 17 Pro models, but if you want more storage, those price increases are even higher.

title: iPhone 18 Pro's Redesigned Vapor Chamber Triples Cooling Surface Area
content:
Apple today announced a redesigned thermal system for iPhone 18 Pro and ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ Max, built around a next-generation vapor chamber with three times the surface area of the one in iPhone 17 Pro.


The new vapor chamber constantly cycles deionized water throughout the system for significantly improved cooling performance, allowing the A20 Pro chip to sustain higher performance for longer under heavy workloads.

Apple redesigned the silicon packaging with "custom packaging inspired by our M-series chips," placing the silicon die and memory side by side rather than stacked, which removes the memory from the chip's thermal path and lets the A20 Pro connect directly to the vapor chamber.

title: iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max Have Different Modems
content:
It looks like the iPhone 18 Pro and ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ Max may have different modems inside. On Apple's technical specifications page for the new devices, the ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ lists Apple's C2 modem, but the ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ Max lists no modem at all in the U.S. 


The same information is also listed on Apple's announcement for the ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ models.
Both models feature N1, an Apple-designed wireless networking chip that enables Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, and Thread. iPhone 18 Pro introduces C2, Apple's next-generation cellular modem system, which brings AI-powered improvements to cellular quality and reliability.

The lack of a C2 mention for the Pro Max might seem like a mistake at first glance, but the separate Pro and Pro Max model numbers actually list different LTE bands. On the U.S. Pro specification list, there's a Band 106, but there's no Band 106 on the Pro Max list.

It is not known why Apple would use different modems for the ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ and ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ Max, but there were rumors before launch that some devices would continue to use Qualcomm modems.

Apple is also using the C2 modem for the iPhone Duo, so it's possible there were supply issues. It appears both the new ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ and ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ Max may use the C2 modem outside of the U.S., so the split could be U.S. only. 

The C2 modem supports both sub-6GHz and mmWave 5G, and Apple says it includes AI improvements to cellular quality and reliability. It is faster and more energy efficient than the C1X modem, but it's not yet clear how it compares to the Qualcomm modem in the 18 Pro Max.

title: iPhone Duo Guide: Everything you need to know about Apple’s folding iPhone
content:
Macworld





The iPhone Duo is Apple’s first foldable iPhone, opening like a book from a compact 5.4-inch phone into a much larger 7.6-inch device. Apple describes the internal screen as its largest-ever iPhone display, with 50 percent more screen area than the iPhone 18 Pro Max, while the outer display provides more than 90 percent of the screen area of an iPhone 18 Pro.
The biggest change is obviously the folding design, but Apple has done more than simply add a hinge. iOS 27 adapts to different positions and orientations, supporting Split View multitasking, hands-free FaceTime and video, StandBy without charging, and layouts that move seamlessly between the two screens. Apple Pencil USB-C support is also coming later in 2026.
The other major changes are the 7.6-inch nano-texture inner display, Touch ID replacing Face ID, an A20 Pro processor with vapor-chamber cooling, and a dual-battery system designed around the two halves of the phone. Apple has also introduced camera features that exploit the second screen, including Duo Preview, Smart Take, Kid Cue and Duo FaceTime.
Much of the pre-launch reporting proved accurate: the Duo name, book-style design, roughly 7.7- and 5.4-inch screens, Touch ID, two 48MP rear cameras, two front-facing cameras, A20 Pro, C2 modem, MagSafe and the white/dark-blue colours were all anticipated.
iPhone Duo at a glance
Apple’s first folding iPhone, with 5.4-inch outer and 7.6-inch inner displays.
Touch ID replaces Face ID, with the fingerprint sensor incorporated into the side button.
A20 Pro with vapor-chamber cooling, including a new 2nm manufacturing process.
Dual-battery architecture, giving up to 44 hours of video playback on the outer display.
Fold-specific iOS and camera features, including Split View, Duo Preview, Smart Take, Kid Cue and hands-free use.
iPhone Duo: Top 10 features


Foldable designBook-style titanium design with precision hinge
Inner display7.6-inch Super Retina XDR OLED, 120Hz ProMotion
Outer display5.4-inch Super Retina XDR OLED, 120Hz ProMotion
ProcessorA20 Pro, 6-core CPU, 7-core GPU
Neural EngineDual 16-core Neural Engine
AuthenticationTouch ID in side button
Rear cameras48MP Main + 48MP Ultra Wide
BatteryDual batteries; up to 44 hours video on outer screen
ConnectivityC2 modem, Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, second-gen UWB
Storage256GB, 512GB, 1TB or 2TB

 






iPhone Duo release date: When will it go on sale?
Apple unveiled the iPhone Duo on September 9, 2026, but unlike the iPhone 18 Pro models it will not arrive in September.
Pre-orders begin on Friday, October 16, at 1pm in the U.K. and 5am Pacific in the U.S. The iPhone Duo officially goes on sale one week later on Friday, October 23 in more than 70 countries and regions, including the U.K., U.S., Canada, Australia, China, France, Germany, India and Japan. A further 28 countries and regions will get it on October 30.
Pre-order iPhone Duo at Apple U.S. 
Pre-order iPhone Duo at Apple U.K. 
It will be available directly from Apple online and through Apple Stores, with carrier availability varying by market.
The late-October launch confirms earlier reports that the folding iPhone could ship later than the iPhone 18 Pro family, although rumors suggesting a delay as late as December proved overly pessimistic.


						

							


iPhone Duo design: What does it look like?

				
					

				
			
The iPhone Duo opens up like a book.

Apple




The iPhone Duo uses a book-style folding design. Closed, it is unusually short and wide for an iPhone, measuring 84.1mm wide, 117.8mm tall and 11.3mm thick. Open it and the width expands to 164.6mm, while thickness reduces to just 5.2mm, making it Apple’s thinnest iPhone when unfolded (taking that mantel from the iPhone Air). It weighs 254g.
The outer screen measures 5.4 inches, while the folding inner panel measures 7.6 inches. Both are Super Retina XDR OLED displays with ProMotion up to 120Hz, Always-On display support and up to 3,000 nits outdoor peak brightness. The internal display also has a nano-texture surface designed to reduce reflections and make the crease less noticeable.
The frame and hinge cover are made from Grade 5 titanium. Apple uses a mirror-polished finish on the enclosure and a micro-blasted finish on the 3D-printed hinge cover. Ceramic Shield protects the rear, while Ceramic Shield 2 protects the outer display. The phone retains an IP68 rating despite its folding construction.

				
					

				
			
The hinge from the outside.

Apple




There are just two colors: Star White and Night Sky, essentially confirming the pre-event reports of silver/white and a very dark blue. For more information read about the iPhone Duo colors.
Action button and Camera Control
There is Camera Control, giving access to exposure, depth, zoom, cameras, styles and tone. It can also launch the new Siri Camera mode.
However, Apple’s Duo doesn’t feature an Action button. The regular iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max retain both the Action button and Camera Control, so this is one hardware-control compromise of the folding model.


						

							


Face ID, Touch ID and the notch
Perhaps the most surprising difference between the iPhone Duo and Apple’s other flagship iPhones is that there is no Face ID.
Instead, Apple has brought back Touch ID, with the fingerprint sensor incorporated into the side button. It works whether the Duo is folded or unfolded, and Apple Watch can also be used to unlock the device. This confirms one of the most persistent pre-launch rumors.
The internal display therefore does not need the TrueDepth sensors used for Face ID. Its FaceTime camera sits beneath the display and disappears when it isn’t being used, giving the inner screen a largely uninterrupted surface.
The inner camera itself is hidden below the display rather than sitting permanently in a visible camera cutout. And yet,despite this and the absence of Face ID, there is still support for Dynamic Island.


						

							




iPhone Duo cameras: What cameras does it have?

				
					

				
			
There are two cameras on the rear.

Apple




The Duo has a 48MP Dual Fusion camera system, comprising:


CameraResolutionEquivalent focal lengthAperture

Fusion Main48MP26mmf/1.6
2x crop from Main12MP52mmf/1.6
Fusion Ultra Wide48MP13mmf/2.2
Outer front camera12MP—f/2.2
Inner FaceTime cameraApple does not specify resolution—f/1.8

 



The Duo does not have variable aperture. Variable aperture is exclusive to the 48MP Fusion Main camera in the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max.


The biggest camera features for iPhone Duo
Duo Preview
The outer screen can show a live preview while somebody else is being photographed, allowing the subject to adjust their pose and framing.
Smart Take and Kid Cue
Smart Take detects when everybody is ready and automatically captures the shot. Kid Cue uses animations on the outer screen to encourage children to look towards the camera.
Two-screen shooting
The folding design supports unusual shooting configurations, including using the main cameras for selfies or group photos while seeing the composition on the other screen. Duo FaceTime can also put nearby participants onto the outer display.
Other notable camera features include 48MP macro photography, a 2x optical-quality crop from the Main camera, an under-display inner FaceTime camera, Dual Capture for simultaneous front-and-rear video, and 4K Dolby Vision recording at up to 120fps.


						

							


Rear cameras
The 48MP Fusion Main has an f/1.6 aperture, sensor-shift stabilization and can shoot 24MP or 48MP images. It also provides a 12MP, 2x optical-quality crop equivalent to a 52mm lens.
The 48MP Fusion Ultra Wide has a 13mm-equivalent lens, f/2.2 aperture and 120-degree field of view. It also supports 48MP macro photography and is the same Ultra Wide camera used by the iPhone 18 Pro family.
That means the Duo does not match the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max camera system. Those phones add a dedicated 48MP Fusion Telephoto and variable aperture on the Main camera, making the Pro models much more flexible for photography despite costing substantially less.
Pre-event reports were divided between a Main + Telephoto and Main + Ultra Wide arrangement. Apple ultimately chose Main + Ultra Wide, confirming the earlier reports that a dedicated telephoto could be sacrificed to save space.
Front cameras
On the outside is a 12MP Center Stage camera with an f/2.2 aperture. It supports Center Stage, automatic portrait/landscape framing, Dual Capture, Photonic Engine, Deep Fusion, Smart HDR 5 and 4K Dolby Vision video at up to 60fps.
Inside is an under-display FaceTime camera with an f/1.8 aperture. Apple does not specify its megapixel resolution. It supports Center Stage for video calls and records at up to 1080p/60fps. Its major advantage is visual rather than photographic: the camera effectively disappears beneath the display when it isn’t being used.
iPhone Duo video features
The Main camera records 4K Dolby Vision at 24, 25, 30, 60, 100 or 120fps, with 4K/120fps also available for slo-mo. Cinematic mode reaches 4K/60fps and Action mode up to 2.8K/60fps. Dual Capture can record at up to 4K/30fps.
Apple’s specifications also do not list ProRes or Apple Log recording for the Duo. Those remain more Pro-oriented capabilities rather than part of Apple’s foldable camera proposition.
The Duo does support Spatial Audio recording, Audio Mix, Dolby Vision HDR and Apple’s computational photography features including Photonic Engine, Deep Fusion, Smart HDR 5, Photographic Styles 3, smart focus tracking and Apple Intelligence-powered editing.
Apple does not list conventional Spatial Video capture in the Duo specifications.


						

							


iPhone Duo processor: What processor does it use?

				
					

				
			
Watch video on the screen.

Apple




The iPhone Duo uses the A20 Pro, the same processor as the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max.
It is manufactured using a 2-nanometer process, a major step forward in transistor density and efficiency. Apple combines it with a new chip packaging design inspired by its M-series Mac processors. The package connects the A20 Pro directly to a custom vapor chamber to transfer heat away from the processor more effectively.
The A20 Pro includes:
6-core CPU: two super cores and four efficiency cores
7-core GPU with Neural Accelerators
Dual 16-core Neural Engine
Hardware-accelerated ray tracing
A dedicated display engine capable of operating both Duo displays
Compared with the A19 Pro, Apple says the CPU is up to 20 percent faster, while the GPU is up to 40 percent faster and more power-efficient. The Dual 16-core Neural Engine delivers twice the compute power, while unified-memory bandwidth rises by 50 percent.
Apple also claims that the complete thermal system gives the Duo up to 35 percent better sustained performance than the iPhone 17 Pro. That sustained-performance figure is particularly important for a folding device because prolonged gaming, multitasking and AI workloads generate considerably more heat than short benchmark bursts.


						

							


iPhone Duo RAM: How much memory does it have?
Apple has not disclosed how much RAM is inside the iPhone Duo.
Before launch, supply-chain reports consistently pointed to 12GB of RAM, which would make sense given the demands of running two displays, simultaneous applications, Siri AI and larger on-device AI models. However, until teardowns or diagnostic tools confirm the figure, 12GB should remain labelled as a rumor rather than an official specification.
Apple does reveal that A20 Pro has 50 percent more unified-memory bandwidth than A19 Pro, which should help the Duo move data more quickly between the CPU, GPU and Neural Engine.
Extra memory is particularly useful on the Duo because iOS 27 can display multiple apps simultaneously and because Apple Intelligence and Siri AI increasingly run generative models locally rather than relying entirely on cloud processing.


						

							


iPhone Duo connectivity

				
					

				
			
An expensive desk calendar. 

Apple




Apple has put a significant amount of its own communications silicon into the iPhone Duo.
It uses Apple’s new C2 cellular modem, replacing Qualcomm silicon. Apple says C2 introduces AI-powered improvements to cellular quality and reliability and supports mmWave 5G in the U.S.
The N1 wireless networking chip provides:
Wi-Fi 7 with 2×2 MIMO
Bluetooth 6
Thread networking
The Duo also has Apple’s second-generation Ultra Wideband chip, NFC and precision dual-frequency GPS.
It is eSIM-only worldwide, something that had been widely rumored before launch. Eliminating the SIM tray gives Apple additional internal space for its batteries.
Satellite capabilities include:
Emergency SOS via satellite
Roadside Assistance via satellite
Find My via satellite
Messages via satellite


						

							


Battery, MagSafe and charging: What’s available?
Instead of one battery spanning the body, the iPhone Duo contains two rechargeable lithium-ion batteries, with one high-energy battery fitted into each half of the device. Apple’s energy-balancing algorithms make them operate as a single battery system.
Apple rates battery life at:
Up to 24 hours of typical use
Up to 44 hours video playback using the outer display
Up to 31 hours using the inner display
Up to 37 hours streamed video on the outer screen
Up to 26 hours streamed video on the inner display
Apple has not disclosed the batteries’ combined capacity in mAh. The pre-launch rumor of approximately 5,000-5,500mAh therefore remains unconfirmed.
Wired charging can take the Duo to 50 percent in around 20 minutes with a 60W-or-higher USB-C adapter.
Despite earlier uncertainty, MagSafe is supported, with wireless charging at up to 25W. Qi2 charging also reaches 25W. Apple says a 35W-or-higher adapter and MagSafe charger can bring the battery to around 50 percent in approximately 30 minutes.


						

							




iPhone Duo price: How much does it cost?
The iPhone Duo starts at $1,999 in the U.S. and £1,999 in the U.K. for 256GB.
Prices are:


StorageStorage

256GB$1,999/£1,999
512GB$2,199/£2,199
1TB$2,599/£2,599
2TB$3,199/£3,199

 



The 256GB starting capacity means Apple has not created an unusually low-storage entry model simply to make the headline price look lower.
iPhone Duo vs iPhone 18 Pro pricing
The iPhone 18 Pro starts at $1,199/£1,199, while the iPhone 18 Pro Max starts at $1,299/£1,299. That makes the Duo approximately $700/£700 more expensive than the Pro Max at entry level.
That premium buys the folding display, precision hinge, titanium structure, second screen and more complex dual-battery design rather than superior cameras: in several areas the iPhone 18 Pro models are actually better equipped.
Reports before the launch suggested the Duo could cost anywhere from around $1,999 to $2,399 at entry level, largely because of the folding OLED display, hinge mechanism, titanium components and other expensive parts. Apple ultimately landed at the very bottom of those predictions.
iPhone Duo vs iPhone 18 Pro pricing
The iPhone 18 Pro starts at $1,199/£1,199, while the iPhone 18 Pro Max starts at $1,299/£1,299. That makes the Duo approximately $700/£700 more expensive than the Pro Max at entry level.
That premium buys the folding display, precision hinge, titanium structure, second screen and more complex dual-battery design rather than superior cameras: in several areas the iPhone 18 Pro models are actually better equipped.
Reports before the launch suggested the Duo could cost anywhere from around $1,999 to $2,399 at entry level, largely because of the folding OLED display, hinge mechanism, titanium components and other expensive parts. Apple ultimately landed at the very bottom of those predictions.
Should you buy the iPhone Duo?
The iPhone Duo is the iPhone to buy if you genuinely want a phone and small tablet in one device. Its 7.6-inch display, multitasking features, A20 Pro performance and clever fold-specific camera modes offer capabilities no other iPhone has. 
But at $1,999/£1,999 it is enormously expensive, and there are significant compromises: no Face ID, no dedicated telephoto camera, no variable aperture and no Action button. 
For photography, battery life and conventional everyday use, the iPhone 18 Pro Max is likely to be the better-value flagship. Buy the Duo because you want the folding experience, not because it is simply the “best” iPhone.

title: iPhone 18 Pro Introduces 'Apple Reference Image' to Verify Photo Authenticity
content:
Apple today announced Apple Reference Image, a new opt-in feature for the iPhone 18 Pro and ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ Max that helps users to prove a photo hasn't been altered since it was taken.



Apple Reference Image is powered by a new sensor in the Main camera that signs sensor data at the pixel level at the moment of capture. When a photo is taken in the new Reference mode, that signed data is sent to Private Cloud Compute, which develops it into what Apple calls an unalterable reference image, "like having a digital negative."

Photos app alongside the corresponding photo, letting users visually compare the two to check whether any edits were made. Apple is also opening APIs in iOS, iPadOS, and macOS 27 so third-party apps can display these reference images.

Apple positioned the feature as one part of a broader push on image authenticity, alongside existing image metadata and upcoming support for the SynthID standard, which will help identify images that were generated or edited with AI. Apple said SynthID support will arrive in a software update later this year and will be included with most edited images, depending on which edits were applied.

iOS 27, iPadOS 27, and macOS 27 will still be able to develop and view reference images.

title: Four features that take the iPhone 18 Pro to the next level
content:
Macworld





At its highly anticipated “Surprise and Shine” event, Apple on Wendesday announced the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max. While the iPhone Duo may have stolen the show with its all-new, foldable form factor, Apple continues to offer its best mobile technology for casual users through the Pro family.
The iPhone 18 Pro’s fresh additions may not be as dramatic or apparent as those of its predecessor. Still, the new flagships pack a ton of welcome upgrades across the line, making them especially enticing for those using older iPhone generations. Some of the most notable iPhone 18 Pro enhancements revolve around core elements, including its screen, main camera lens, processor, and more. Here are the new features that take the iPhone 18 Pro to the next level.


Professional camera
Perhaps the most significant introduction to the iPhone Pro line is the all-new variable aperture lens, similar to DSLR and mirrorless cameras. The iPhone 18 Pro’s wide camera now features six laser-cut blades bound to a rotor mechanism, controlling how much light reaches the sensor. In dark environments, you can widen the opening to produce crisper shots, and Night mode works faster. Conversely, the blades close in lighter setups to minimize overexposure. The Camera app allows you to pick between four aperture settings, and third-party camera app developers can bring this functionality via a dedicated API.

				
					

				
			The new variable aperture offers better control to the photographer.
Apple




In the video department, iPhone 18 Pro users can now apply Cinematic effects to 60 fps videos after they’ve been shot. Previously, you needed to pick the dedicated Cinematic mode before hitting the record button. This isolates subjects by blurring the background in a professional-looking manner. Otherwise, Time-lapse recording now supports 4K with stabilization and Dolby Vision HDR. Low-light video has also been improved, along with the algorithms that power the Audio Mix feature—which can now detect music.
Advanced camera hardware requires matching software, and the iPhone 18 Pro models take that into account. The devices offer a revamped Camera app with support for Pro controls. These let you easily adjust the white balance, aperture, shutter speed, and more. You could also view a histogram to check the exposure levels. Casual users will also appreciate Photographic Styles 3.0, which unlock texture and grain controls.


						

							


Supercharged by A20 Pro
It goes without saying that the new iPhones pack a brand-new mobile chip. The 2-nanometer A20 Pro processor features six CPU cores, including two super cores and four efficiency ones. The GPU goes for seven cores and boasts up to 40 percent faster speeds compared to last year’s A19 Pro. In the AI department, the dual 16-core Neural Engine offers double the processing power for AI tasks, such as Siri AI and computational photography. Combined, these upgrades contribute to a 50 percent increase in memory bandwidth, unlocking desktop-class computing on the latest iPhones.

				
					

				
			

Apple




To maximize the A20 Pro’s efficiency, the iPhone 18 Pro introduces an overhauled vapor chamber with triple the surface area. The SoC is now directly connected to it, increasing its thermo-management efficacy. Not only does this minimize processor throttling but it also helps limit energy overuse. As such, the new models offer the longest battery life to date, with the iPhone 18 Pro lasting for 36 hours and the 18 Pro Max stretching it to 45 hours when playing video on a single charge. Charging an iPhone 18 Pro to 50 percent takes around 15 or 30 minutes when opting for wired or wireless chargers, respectively. Meanwhile, a 5-minute wired charging session can provide around seven hours of video playback on the iPhone 18 Pro Max.


						

							



Dynamic Island 2.0
Another welcome iPhone 18 Pro change is the smaller Dynamic Island cutout. Not only does this make the device more immersive, but it also upgrades its functionality. Previously limited to up to two Live Activities, the shrunken Dynamic Island on the latest models can fit up to three. This allows you to easily glance at several ongoing events, like order tracking, flight status, timer progress, and much more.

				
					

				
			
Apple



							



Cherry picking season
Lastly, the iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max build upon last year’s dramatic exterior redesign. The back glass panel’s color now matches that of the aluminum body, contributing to a more cohesive look. The finishes have also been refined and expanded, letting you pick between Black, Silver, Glacier, and the soon-to-be-fan-favorite, Burgundy.


						

							





The iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max start at $1,199 and $1,299 for the base variants with 256GB of storage–a $100 price increase compared to last year’s release. You can pre-order one beginning Saturday, September 12, with general availability to follow on Friday, September 18.
