title: iPhone Duo: The 5 most important things you need to know
content:
Macworld





After years of rumors, leaks, and speculation, the folding iPhone is finally here. This project has been reported on for so long that our first article about it dates to 2018! Its name is iPhone Duo—not iPhone Ultra as previously expected—and there will be a lot to say about it over the coming weeks before and after its release on October 23.
But for now, here are the five most important things you need to know about iPhone Duo.
$1,999, two colors, mid-October
As expected, the iPhone Duo is about twice the price of an iPhone 17 Pro. The starting price is $1,999 with 256GB of storage, which is actually on the lower side of the rumors. Adding more storage inflates the price, with options up to 2 terabytes for $3,199.
Preorders start on October 16, and the iPhone Duo goes on sale on October 23.
There are two colors available: Star White and Night Sky. These are very similar to the Silver and Midnight colors we’ve seen in previous Apple products.

				
					

				
			
Apple




It’s all about flexibility
One thing the rumors didn’t pick up on: Both the inner and outer displays have the same aspect ratio: 1:1.4. That makes the outer display exactly one half of the inner display, and Apple uses this symmetry, along with a lot of orientation sensing, to alter the way iOS works.

				
					

				
			
Apple




Currently, many iOS apps, and the operating system itself, do not adjust to multiple orientations. With the Duo, Apple has updated its own apps to work in portrait or landscape, and even behave differently depending on whether they’re on the outside or inside screen.

				
					

				
			The inner display shows two home screens at once, and the dock is on the side.
Apple




The Dock now runs up the side of the screen, allowing more vertical room for the Home Screen, and the inside display simply shows two home screens at once. Most app toolbars and controls are also now on the side edge, along with a new more compact status icon area.
Speakers are on the top and bottom, so no matter which way you hold the iPhone Duo, open or closed, you get proper sound orientation and stereo separation.

				
					

				
			
Apple




The trick is that apps can adapt to present themselves to both the dual-screen nature and shifting orientations of iPhone Duo. You can show your FaceTime call on the outer display as well as the inside, so other people can see and participate in the call. You can partially fold the phone and use it that way and the interface reacts. Fold it like a tent and it goes into Standby mode to show big clock, calendar, photo, and weather widgets–even when you’re not charging. Apple even showed a quick glimpse of the Duo acting like a tiny laptop with touchscreen keys.

				
					

				
			Fold the Duo over and it goes into Standby mode, even when not charging.
Apple




And of course, you can run two apps side by side, or even two instances of the same app in some cases. Plus, you can save “married” apps for easy access later. And later this year, you’ll even be able to use the USB-C Apple Pencil on both the inner and outer displays.
The focus is on letting you use both the inner and outer displays in all sorts of flexible ways.
A new camera experience
The two outside cameras are 48 megapixel wide and ultra-wide. It’s not the new variable-aperture camera of the iPhone 18 Pro and there’s no telephoto, as expected. But there are a few software tricks up Apple’s sleeve.
iPhone Duo reacts to being propped up or folded in various ways to let you do unique things, like take selfies with the outside cameras while it is unfolded, using the outer display to show you the shot.
Fold it halfway to prop the camera up and step back to take shots with the new Smart Take feature that automatically takes the shot when everyone is posed and ready instead of relying on a strict timer.

				
					

				
			You can  mirror your FaceTime call to the outer display so others can participate, too.
Apple




And the new FaceTime camera on the inside is now under the display, so it disappears entirely when you’re not using it.
There’s even a new Kid Cue feature that plays Peanuts animations on the outer display to grab your child’s attention, so they looks at the camera when you’re trying to take their picture.
A focus on durability and display quality
Apple has clearly heard complaints about other folding phones and has given Duo a polished titanium frame, and an ultra-precise hinge design using over 100 elements. Embedded magnets give you that satisfying “click” when you close it and keep it shut.
The result is an IP68 water and dust rating, which is a lot better than we’ve seen from most other foldable phones and equivalent to other recent iPhones.

				
					

				
			Apple spent years perfecting the Duo’s hinge.
Apple




Apple went to great lengths to highlight the superiority of its inner display. It uses a new nano-texture matte finish that helps make the crease harder to notice, and a multi-layer bonding process for durability and to make the display fully flat so you don’t get that annoying waviness or creasing you sometimes see with foldable phones.

				
					

				
			The multiple display layers slide past each other like pages on a book, to reduce warping and waves.
Apple




A20 Pro and C2 modem, and battery life
The A20 Pro is at the heart of the iPhone Duo, and it’s just like the one in the iPhone 18 Pro–there aren’t any disabled GPU cores or anything like that.
Sustained performance will be a little lower because cooling the chip is more challenging, but it will still be much faster than the iPhone 17 Pro—up to 35% higher sustained performance, according to Apple.
Like the iPhone 18 Pro, the iPhone Duo also includes both Apple’s N1 chip for Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6, and the new C2 modem. Apple says the new modem provides better reliability and efficiency, 50 percent faster uploads, and supports mmWave in the United States.
Both halves of the iPhone Fold have a high-density battery, which gives it very good battery life specs. Apple says you can expect up to 44 hours of video playback on the outer display, and 31 hours on the inner display. That falls right in between the battery life of an iPhone 17 and iPhone 17 Pro, and is quite a bit longer than the iPhone Air.
And yes, MagSafe and Qi wireless charging are still supported.

title: iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Duo Feature Apple's New C2 Modem [Updated]
content:
Apple today unveiled new iPhone 18 Pro models and the iPhone Duo – the company's first foldable iPhone – and both the iPhone 18 Pro and the iPhone Duo feature Apple's new custom-designed C2 modem for 5G connectivity.


Prior to today's announcements, there was speculation that Apple's C2 in-house modem would not support mmWave 5G in the U.S., and that the company would once again rely on Qualcomm to fill the gap for American carriers. Apparently, that's not the case, at least as far mmWave support goes.

Apple's press release for the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max and the tech specs page for the two models appear to indicate that the C2 modem is limited to only the smaller iPhone 18 Pro model, leaving the iPhone 18 Pro Max on Qualcomm modems. The reason for the distinction is unclear given the near identical capabilities of the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max.

Apple says the C2 brings AI-powered improvements to cellular quality and reliability, and now supports mmWave in the U.S. The company claims the C2 also delivers meaningfully faster uploads when compared to C1X while consuming 15 percent less energy.

As for mmWave support, Apple's U.S. specifications list bands n258, n260, and n261, alongside sub-6GHz 5G with 4×4 MIMO, but the UK specifications list sub-6GHz only.

Meanwhile, both models feature the N1, an Apple-designed wireless networking chip that enables Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, and Thread support.

The iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max come in burgundy, glacier, silver, and black colors, with prices starting at $1,199 and $1,299, respectively. Both models come in 256GB, 512GB, 1TB, and 2TB storage options and will be available to order September 12.

iPhone Duo is available in star white and night sky colors, and starts at $1,999, coming in 256GB, 512GB, 1TB, and 2TB storage capacities. Pre-orders for the iPhone Duo begin on Friday, October 16, with availability beginning Friday, October 23.

Update: This article originally stated that all three models include the C2 modem, but it appears the iPhone 18 Pro Max does not in fact include it.

title: AirPods 5: The 5 coolest features Apple announced
content:
Macworld





Apple introduced the AirPods 5 during its Surprise and Shine event on Wednesday. Apple’s popular earphones have a very similar design to the model they replace, but they feature several internal improvements over the AirPods 4. Here are five things you need to know about the new AirPods 5.


Better Active Noise Cancellation
Apple introduced Active Noise Cancellation to the entry-level AirPods with the AirPods 4 in 2024, a welcome feature for anyone who prefers open-air earphones instead of in-ear ones such as the AirPods Pro. On the AirPods 5, the ANC has gotten even better, thanks to a “new multi-port acoustic architecture and improved computational audio algorithms.” Apple claims that the AirPods 5 removes up to 50 percent more noise compared to the AirPods 4.
Apple also improved Transparency mode so that voices and sounds are more natural. The Adaptive Audio feature tracks the sound in your environment and automatically switches between ANC and Transparency modes.


						

							


Active Noise Cancellation is now standard
Active Noise Cancellation is now a standard feature for the AirPods, meaning you can’t get a model without it, as was the case with AirPods 4. So you no longer have to shop and ponder if you really need ANC or not–if you don’t want to use it, then simply turn it off.


						

							


Improved sound quality
That new multiport acoustic architecture that improved ANC also works with a “next-generation Adaptive EQ” to generate better sound across “an even wider range of ear geometries,” according to Apple’s announcement. This also makes Personalized Spatial Audio sound more immersive.

				
					

				
			
Apple made improvements that result in better sound from the AirPods 5.

Apple



							


Better battery life
The AirPods 5 are rated at 4 hours of playback on a single charge with ANC active, which is technically one hour less than the AirPods 4 with ANC. However, the testing methods are different. As Apple explains, AirPods 4 with Active Noise Cancellation were tested with Active Noise Cancellation turned off, while AirPods 5 were tested with Active Noise Cancellation turned on. With Noise Control turned off, Apple says you’ll get up to 7 hours of listening on the AirPods 5.


						

							


The price
The AirPods 5 with a USB-C charging case is $129, which is the same as the AirPods 4 without ANC, effectively a $50 price cut over AirPods 4 with ANC. In this era of increasing prices, this is a great surprise.
One caveat, however. The $129 AirPods now come with a wired charging case, which means you need to plug it in to charge it. If that’s a nuisance, Apple offers the AirPods 5 with a wireless charging case for $149 (and you’ll also get volume controls built into the stems like AirPods Pro). So, the AirPods 5 (with ANC standard) and the wireless charging case are still $30 cheaper than the AirPods 4 with ANC. Cool.


						

							




The AirPods 5 are available for pre-order now, with shipments starting on September 18.

title: iPhone 18 Pro & Max Guide: Everything you need to know about the new iPhones
content:
Macworld





Apple has unveiled the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max. They retain the 6.3-inch and 6.9-inch screen sizes and aluminium unibody design introduced with the previous generation, but Apple has made substantial changes to the cameras, processor, cooling, battery life and connectivity.
The biggest camera upgrade is a new 48MP Fusion Main camera with variable aperture, which can automatically move between ƒ/1.48, ƒ/1.8, ƒ/2.8 and ƒ/4 depending on lighting and depth of field. Apple says the widest aperture delivers around 50% better low-light performance, while new Pro controls add manual aperture, shutter speed, white balance and histogram controls.
Inside is the A20 Pro, Apple’s first iPhone chip made using a 2nm process. It has a new six-core CPU, seven-core GPU, Dual 16-core Neural Engine and 50% more memory bandwidth than the A19 Pro. A larger vapor chamber and new M-series-inspired chip packaging also improve heat dissipation, with Apple claiming up to 40% better sustained performance than the iPhone 17 Pro.
The other major changes are battery life of up to 36 hours on the Pro and 45 hours on the Pro Max, faster wired charging, the new Apple-designed C2 cellular modem, and a redesigned Dynamic Island capable of showing three Live Activities simultaneously. 
iPhone 18 Pro/Max vs iPhone 17 Pro/Max: Top 10 changes at a glance
The five biggest changes are the variable-aperture camera, A20 Pro, improved cooling, longer battery life and redesigned Dynamic Island/connectivity system. Here is an overview of what’s new compared to the previous generation.

Apple has added a 2TB option to the smaller Pro for the first time, while retaining 256GB as the entry-level capacity.


iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Max release date: When will the new iPhones go on sale?
The iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max were announced on Wednesday, September 9, 2026.
Pre-orders start at 5 a.m. Pacific on Saturday, September 12. That’s 1pm in the U.K.

Pre-order iPhone 18 Pro and Max at Apple U.K. 
Both models will then go on sale on Friday, September 18, 2026 in more than 65 countries and regions. Another 20 countries will get the phones from September 25.
You will be able to buy the phones directly from Apple online or at Apple Stores, as well as through mobile networks and authorized Apple retailers. Apple sells unlocked iPhones directly through its website and stores.


						

							


iPhone 18 Pro/Max design: What does it look like?

				
					

				
			
This is the Burgundy variant (we think Deep Cherry was a much nicer name).

Apple




The iPhone 18 Pro retains the aluminium unibody introduced with the iPhone 17 Pro, as well as the Ceramic Shield on the rear and Ceramic Shield 2 over the display. The camera system remains arranged on the large raised plateau across the upper part of the rear casing.
Screen sizes are unchanged at 6.3 inches for the iPhone 18 Pro and 6.9 inches for the iPhone 18 Pro Max, both using Super Retina XDR OLED displays with ProMotion up to 120Hz.

Glacier

That means Cosmic Orange and Deep Blue disappear, while black returns to the Pro line despite pre-launch reports suggesting it would not. REad more about the color choices here: Apple’s new iPhone 18 Pro colors.
The pre-event leaks suggested the basic chassis dimensions would remain very close to the iPhone 17 Pro and Pro Max, with the camera plateau rather than the body itself becoming thicker. 
The new iPhones share the same screen sizes and overall form as their predecessors, but both models are slightly heavier this time. 
iPhone 18 Pro dimensions: 150 x 71.9 x 8.75mm / 5.91 x 2.83 x 0.34 in
iPhone 18 Pro weight: 7.44 ounces / 211 grams (17 Pro was 7.27 ounces / 206 grams)
iPhone 18 Pro Max dimensions: 163.4 x 78 x 8.75mm / 6.43 x 3.07 x 0.34 in
iPhone 18 Pro Max weight: 8.78 ounces / 249 grams (17 Pro Max was 8.22 ounces / 233 grams)
Changes to the Dynamic Island
Apple has redesigned the Dynamic Island. Apple says new display technology creates additional usable space and allows the Dynamic Island to display up to three Live Activities at once, for example navigation, music and a sports score.
Apple has not announced fully under-display Face ID. Pre-launch reports suggested that one or more infrared Face ID components could move beneath the OLED panel, allowing the notch to shrink, but Apple hasn’t confirmed the underlying sensor arrangement.


						

							


iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max cameras: Are the cameras the same?

				
					

				
			
The iPhone 18 Pro cameras.

Apple




Both the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max have the same three-camera rear system. The main change is not resolution—all three remain 48MP—but the new variable-aperture Main camera and new computational imaging pipeline.
The three most notable camera upgrades are:
Variable aperture on the 48MP Main camera.
A new Main camera sensor and imaging pipeline, improving low-light performance and detail.
More extensive manual Pro controls, including aperture, shutter speed, white balance and histogram.


						

							




Rear cameras

The Main camera’s six-blade mechanical aperture can automatically open to ƒ/1.48 in low light or close as far as ƒ/4 for increased depth of field. Apple says the widest setting improves low-light performance by around 50%. Photographers can also select aperture manually.
Both Pro models also offer up to 8x optical-quality zoom from the Telephoto camera. Contrary to some earlier rumors, the variable-aperture camera is not exclusive to the Pro Max.


Front camera
Apple has retained the 18MP Center Stage front camera, rather than moving to the rumored 24MP sensor. It supports automatic reframing, Center Stage, ultra-stabilized video and Dual Capture.
The front camera remains visibly associated with the Dynamic Island. Apple has not announced an under-display selfie camera on the iPhone 18 Pro.
iPhone 18 Pro video changes
Frame rates: Cinematic effects can now be applied after shooting to ordinary videos captured at up to 60fps. The phones continue to offer 4K 120fps Dolby Vision for high-frame-rate shooting.
Time-lapse: Time-lapse receives a significant upgrade to 4K with Dolby Vision HDR.
Computational photography: Apple has introduced a new imaging pipeline, smart focus tracking, improved Clean Up, Spatial Reframing, an Extend tool and Photographic Styles 3, which adds texture and grain adjustments.


						

							


A20 Pro processor: How fast is it?

				
					

				
			
Apple has redesigned the iPhone chip. 

Apple




Both the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max use Apple’s new A20 Pro processor.
It is manufactured using a 2-nanometer process, down from the 3nm-class process used for A19 Pro, giving Apple more scope to improve efficiency and transistor density.
The chip includes:
6-core CPU
7-core GPU
Neural Accelerators integrated into the CPU/GPU architecture
Dual 16-core Neural Engine, 32 cores in total
50% more memory bandwidth than A19 Pro
Apple says the GPU is up to 40% faster than A19 Pro, while the Neural Engine offers roughly double the AI processing capability.
One particularly important change is the packaging. Inspired by Apple’s M-series Mac chips, A20 Pro places the processor die side-by-side with memory rather than stacking memory directly in the chip’s thermal path. This improves heat transfer and allows the processor to couple more directly to the vapor chamber.
That vapor chamber itself has three times the surface area of the iPhone 17 Pro’s system. Apple claims the combination delivers up to 40% better sustained performance, which should be most noticeable during gaming, video work and intensive on-device AI rather than ordinary web browsing and messaging.


						

							


RAM: How much memory does the iPhone 18 Pro/Max have?
Apple does not officially publish RAM capacities for iPhones, and its launch material does not specify a RAM figure.
Reports ahead of the event indicated 12GB of RAM, but importantly the iPhone 17 Pro was also widely reported to have 12GB. That means there may not be a capacity increase this generation.
The more important confirmed improvement is 50% higher memory bandwidth, which allows the A20 Pro, GPU and Neural Engine to access data faster.
That is particularly relevant to Apple Intelligence and Siri AI. Larger on-device AI models demand not only sufficient RAM but very high memory bandwidth, so Apple’s chip and packaging changes should allow more complex models to run locally and for longer without the same thermal constraints.


						

							


iPhone 18 Pro/Max connectivity options 
C2 modem
One of the biggest changes is Apple’s C2 cellular modem, replacing the Qualcomm modem used in the previous Pro generation.
Apple says C2 delivers:
Faster upload performance than C1X
15% lower energy consumption
AI-powered improvements to connection quality and reliability
mmWave support in the U.S.
This confirms a major rumor from before the launch.
Wi-Fi and Bluetooth
Like the predecessors, the 2026 iPhones use Apple’s N1 wireless networking chip, supporting:
Wi-Fi 7
Bluetooth 6
Thread
Satellite
Emergency SOS via satellite, Messages via satellite, Roadside Assistance via satellite and Find My satellite functionality continue. Apple made no announcements about full satellite internet or ordinary 5G data delivered by satellite, despite pre-launch rumors suggesting such a capability could appear.


						

							


iPhone 18 Pro/Max Battery, MagSafe and charging: What’s changed?
Battery life is one of the most significant improvements.
Apple says eSIM-only models gain additional battery capacity because the space previously occupied by the physical SIM tray can be used for battery cells. Physical-SIM variants provide around two hours less video playback than equivalent eSIM-only models.
The improvement comes from a combination of larger batteries, the more efficient 2nm A20 Pro processor and lower-power C2 modem.


						

							




Apple rates eSIM-only models for up to:


ModeliPhone 18iPhone 17Improvement
Pro36 hours video playback33 hoursUp to +3 hours
Pro Max45 hours video playback39 hours+6 hours

 






Wired charging
Wired charging is faster. The iPhone 18 Pro can reach 50% in around 15 minutes, compared with around 20 minutes for the iPhone 17 Pro. Five minutes of wired charging can provide around seven hours of video playback on the Pro Max.
MagSafe and wireless charging
Wireless charging can reach 50% in around 30 minutes, which is broadly unchanged from the iPhone 17 Pro generation. There is therefore a wired-charging speed improvement, but Apple hasn’t announced a comparable jump in MagSafe charging speed.


						

							




iPhone 18 Pro price: How much does it cost?
Apple has increased prices by $100 in the U.S. and £100 in the U.K. 
The iPhone 18 Pro starts at $1,199/£1,199, while the iPhone 18 Pro Max starts at $1,299/£1,299. Both begin with 256GB of storage.


ModeliPhone 18 starting priceiPhone 17 starting priceChange
iPhone Pro$1,199/£1,199$1,099/£1,099+$100/£100
iPhone Pro Max$1,299/£1,299$1,199/£1,199+$100/£100

 



Apple offers both models with 256GB, 512GB, 1TB and 2TB. That means the entry-level storage remains 256GB rather than increasing again. The notable change is that 2TB is now available on both models; previously the iPhone 17 Pro topped out at 1TB while the Pro Max could be configured with 2TB.
The $100 increase is considerably smaller than some analyst predictions before launch. Those forecasts had pointed to sharply higher DRAM and NAND costs caused by the global memory shortage, with estimates that the cost of 12GB of DRAM alone could rise dramatically this year. That makes component and memory pricing a credible contributor to Apple’s increase, although Apple itself hasn’t attributed the higher price to any one component.
Should you buy the iPhone 18 Pro or Pro Max? Which model should you choose?

				
					

				
			
Which one do you want?

Apple




The iPhone 18 Pro is a much stronger upgrade than the specifications initially suggest. The variable-aperture camera, A20 Pro, improved cooling, faster charging and better battery life all make meaningful differences, particularly for photography, gaming and intensive AI use. iPhone 17 Pro owners don’t need to rush to upgrade unless those features matter, but anyone coming from an iPhone 15 Pro or older will see a substantial jump. The 6.3-inch Pro is the better choice for most buyers because it has the same cameras and processor. Choose the Pro Max mainly if you want its larger display and class-leading 45-hour video battery life.
Did Apple launch the iPhone 18? 
There was no new iPhone 18 at the event. We expect the iPhone 18 to launch alongside the iPhone 18e and iPhone Air 2 in spring 2027. Read more about the iPhone 18 here: iPhone 18 and iPhone 18e: Release date, rumored specs and more.

The new iPhones that Apple introduced are more expensive than the models they replaced. And even the old ones all cost more too.

title: Siri on Apple Watch can remember useful parts of your day without retaining everything
content:
Your Apple Watch now listens all day to build a daily Siri Recap from the sounds around you. The catch? It actually forgets the audio the moment it understands the context.

Siri Recap
Audio Intelligence uses Sound Recognition to identify relevant information from the wearer's surroundings as events happen. Siri can combine those signals with other available data to summarize the day later.
Sound Recognition can identify events such as sirens, alarms, doorbells, and a crying baby, giving the system potential safety and accessibility uses. A separate Live Rewind feature lets users double-press the Digital Crown to replay the previous 15 seconds of detected audio and view a transcript.
The resulting Siri Recap doesn't include transcripts of overheard conversations, and Apple says the feature doesn't store audio. Sound processing happens continuously before the original audio is discarded.

title: macOS 27 Golden Gate: New features, release date, beta, compatible Macs
content:
Macworld





Apple has already revealed many of the new features coming in macOS 27 Golden Gate, the next major update for the Mac. Headline changes include an all-new Siri AI assistant, major upgrades to apps including Safari, Photos, Messages, Mail and Calendar, expanded child-safety features, design refinements and performance improvements throughout the operating system. We’ve also had the chance to see many of these features in action through the beta. Now the full release is only days away with Apple confirming it will be available from Monday September 14. 
Golden Gate continues Apple’s tradition of naming macOS releases after iconic Californian landmarks. More broadly, the update represents another step in Apple’s push to make the Mac smarter and more proactive, with greater use of Apple Intelligence across the operating system and a stronger focus on helping users complete everyday tasks more quickly.
macOS 27 will support all Macs powered by Apple silicon, marking the end of the road for Intel-based Macs. While Intel models won’t be eligible for the new operating system, Apple is expected to continue providing security updates for them for some time.
This hub covers everything you need to know about macOS 27 Golden Gate, including its new features, compatibility, beta releases and Apple Intelligence upgrades.


What’s New in macOS 27 Golden Gate at a glance

				
					

				
			
Apple




Here are the top ten new features and changes coming with macOS 27 Golden Gate. 
Siri AI: A redesigned conversational Siri that can answer questions, understand personal and onscreen context, access the web and take actions across apps.
Apple Intelligence: Systemwide proofreading, smarter writing tools, improved dictation and automatic file and folder naming.
Safari upgrades: Automatic tab grouping, webpage change alerts with Notify Me, AI-generated extensions and faster, more efficient browsing.
Smarter Messages and Mail: Personalized Smart Reply, better search and syncing, contextual suggestions and improved reliability.
New Photos tools: Spatial Reframing, image expansion with Extend, improved Clean Up and better search and organisation.
More powerful built-in apps: New features for Passwords, Calendar, Notes, Preview, Freeform, Weather, Shortcuts and Image Playground.
Expanded parental controls: Ask to Browse, improved Screen Time, contact approvals and broader Communication Safety protections.
Better Mac gaming: Game Porting Toolkit 4 promises significant performance and compatibility improvements for Windows games.
Refined Liquid Glass design: Better readability and consistency, adjustable transparency, cleaner Finder windows and improved iPhone Mirroring.
Faster macOS performance: Quicker app launches, Spotlight, AirDrop and networking, plus improved external-display, Thunderbolt and Bluetooth support.


						

							


macOS 27 release date: When will macOS 27 be available?
September 14, 2026
macOS 27 has been in beta since it was unveiled at WWDC in June, but the official version of macOS 27 will be available to install on compatible Macs on September 14


						

							


macOS 27 Beta – What’s new in the latest beta?
Latest beta: Release Candidate, September 9, 2026

				
					

				
			

Apple




Apple released the first macOS 27 developer beta at WWDC, followed by the first public beta on July 13, 2026. The current version is the developer release candidate, released on September 9.
At this stage, Apple is mainly refining the software ahead of its expected September release. Recent betas focus on Siri AI, faster performance and search, Safari automation, deeper Apple Intelligence integration and further refinements to Liquid Glass.
Most people should still wait for the final release, particularly if they rely on their Mac for work or use specialist software. Beta software can still cause crashes, app compatibility problems, increased battery drain and, in some cases, data loss. If you do install it, make a full backup first and ideally use a secondary Mac, separate volume or external SSD.
Here’s how you can participate in the beta program we also recommend reading our guide to whether you should install the latest macOS beta.


						

							


Siri AI: Siri powered macOS 27 features  

				
					

				
			
Foiundry




Apple’s biggest focus in macOS 27 Golden Gate is Siri AI, a completely redesigned version of Siri powered by Apple Intelligence. Rather than functioning primarily as a voice assistant, Siri is becoming a conversational AI that can answer questions, understand personal and onscreen context, access current information from the web and take actions across apps.
We tested Siri AI in beta on a MacBook Neo, and it behaves much more like a generative-AI chatbot than the Siri of old. It can answer questions directly, understand natural follow-ups and solve problems instead of simply directing users to web searches.
At a glance: What’s new with Siri AI?
Conversational AI assistant: Siri can handle open-ended questions, brainstorming, research and natural back-and-forth conversations.
Dedicated Siri app: A standalone Siri app keeps conversations in one place and syncs them through iCloud, allowing users to start a conversation on one Apple device and continue it on another.
Personal context awareness: Siri will be able to understand information in Messages, Mail, Notes, Photos, Maps and files to locate information and provide answers based on your personal data.
Web-powered answers: Siri can access current information from the web, making it more useful for research, learning, interview preparation and questions about recent events.
App actions and automation: Siri can perform tasks across apps such as Messages, Music, Reminders, Calendar and Maps using natural-language instructions.
Spotlight integration: Siri AI is integrated with Spotlight, allowing users to type questions and receive AI-generated answers without opening a browser or separate app.
Visual Intelligence: Visual Intelligence comes to the Mac for the first time, allowing Siri to understand selected images, documents, files, text and other content displayed on screen.

				
					

				
			
Apple’s Visual Intelligence initially placed Blutenburg in Denmark.

Macwelt




Writing Tools: Siri can generate text, rewrite drafts, summarise content and adjust wording or tone. Apple says it can also adapt writing to the way you typically communicate with particular contacts.
Improved dictation: Systemwide dictation gains better speech recognition along with automatic punctuation, capitalisation and formatting.
Custom Siri voices: Users can choose Siri’s voice and adjust characteristics such as pace and expressiveness, although some of these capabilities require newer hardware.
macOS 27 also contains an experimental Siri AI popover seen in the beta. Selecting text can bring up a small Siri icon offering contextual actions including Writing Tools, summaries and key points, sending messages or emails, creating calendar events, opening locations in Maps, and tracking flights or packages. The feature is not currently enabled by default and requires Apple’s FeatureFlags system to activate, suggesting it may still be under development.
Apple also appears to be taking a relatively restrained approach to AI behaviour. In our testing, Siri avoids presenting itself as human, excessive flattery and potentially harmful responses, while generally keeping its answers straightforward.
When will Siri AI be available on Mac? 
Siri AI is already available in beta, and Apple says it will be released to the public “later this year.” We therefore expect it to arrive as an update to macOS 27 and Apple’s other OS 27 releases rather than as part of the initial launch.
Apple has also said Siri AI will still be labelled as a beta when it launches, so users should expect some rough edges and continued improvements after release. 
Siri AI is initially available in English. Availability will vary by region. Siri AI will not initially be available on iPhone or iPad in the European Union because of issues related to the Digital Markets Act, and it will remain unavailable in China while Apple works through regulatory approvals. However, it will be available on Mac and Vision Pro in the EU.
Which Macs support Siri AI?
Siri AI requires a Mac that supports Apple Intelligence, but some of its most advanced capabilities have higher hardware requirements.
Apple says its most powerful on-device AI model, expressive Siri voices and advanced dictation require an M3 or later Mac with at least 12GB of unified memory. Macs that support Apple Intelligence but do not meet those requirements can still receive other Siri AI features, although the exact feature set may vary.


						

							


Safari features coming in macOS 27

				
					

				
			
Notify Me in Safari

Apple




Safari is getting several Apple Intelligence-powered upgrades in macOS 27, including smarter tab organisation, webpage monitoring, custom extension generation and performance improvements.
Automatic Tab Topics: Safari will automatically group related tabs by topic as you browse, helping keep research and projects organised. These groups can also be saved for later.
Notify Me: Safari will be able to monitor webpages for changes and alert you when something happens, such as a product coming back in stock or a price dropping, removing the need to keep refreshing pages manually.
Describe an Extension: Users will be able to create custom Safari extensions simply by describing what they want. Safari will generate the extension from the text description and add it to the toolbar.
Faster, more efficient browsing: Apple says Safari will use less power while improving page-loading speed, JavaScript performance, scrolling, animations and resizing of the Start Page.

				
					

				
			
Get notified. 

Macwelt



							


Messages and Mail features coming in macOS 27
Messages and Mail are gaining deeper Apple Intelligence integration in macOS 27, alongside improvements to search, syncing and everyday reliability.
Messages
One-Tap Suggestions in Messages: Messages will suggest useful actions based on the context of a conversation, such as creating a reminder or note without leaving the chat.
Smarter Photo Suggestions: Messages will surface relevant photos based on people, places and keywords mentioned in a conversation.
Personalized Smart Reply: Suggested replies can reflect your usual writing style and adapt depending on who you’re messaging.
Improved syncing: Messages should sync more reliably across devices, while failed messages will automatically retry sending.
Mail
Personalized Smart Reply: Mail will also generate suggested responses that better match your writing style and the person you’re replying to.
More relevant search: A new ranking system will prioritise the most useful search results, alongside improved search indexing.
Faster and more accurate: Apple says Mail will load messages more quickly and provide more reliable unread counts.


						

							


Photos features coming in macOS 27
Photos is gaining new AI-powered editing and organisation tools in macOS 27, making it easier to improve images, find photos and manage an iCloud library.
Spatial Reframing: Photos will be able to intelligently recompose and reframe images after they’ve been taken.
Extend Tool: A new Extend tool can expand an image beyond its original boundaries, filling in missing areas when changing the crop or aspect ratio.
Enhanced Clean Up: Apple’s Clean Up tool will be better at removing larger unwanted objects and distractions from photos.
Better organisation and search: Photos adds keywords, star ratings, improved metadata search and other tools for organising a library.
Faster iCloud syncing: iCloud Photos can begin uploads more quickly, with an option to prioritise syncing when needed.


						

							


Other new features coming to apps with macOS 27
macOS 27 also brings a wide range of smaller upgrades across Apple’s built-in apps, with a particular focus on automation, organisation, security and Apple Intelligence.
Passwords
The Passwords app can automatically identify weak or compromised passwords and, with Apple Intelligence, visit supported websites, change the password and save the new credentials. This could remove much of the manual work involved in updating large numbers of old or leaked passwords, although questions remain over website compatibility, two-factor authentication and how consistently the feature will work. Read: Apple finally got rid of my biggest password headache.
Image Playground
Image Playground gets a substantial AI upgrade, including the ability to create photorealistic images and make more convincing edits to existing pictures, such as changing colours, hair and other details. Apple continues to apply safeguards around real people, copyrighted characters and distinctive artistic styles.

				
					

				
			
Foundry




Calendar
Calendar gains natural-language event creation, making it possible to describe an event rather than manually entering every detail. It can also make changes to multiple events at once.
Preview
Preview supports more document formats, improves PDF editing and saves PDF files more quickly.
Notes
Notes gains drawing tools for sketching with a mouse or trackpad, along with digital signatures, Markdown copy-and-paste and links to sections within notes.

				
					

				
			
Notes now features a drawing tool as well as the ability to create and use digital signatures.

Foundry




Freeform
Freeform adds drawing tools, collaborative folders and improved organisation, including the ability to sort boards into folders. Full dark-mode support also changes the appearance of the drawing canvas.

				
					

				
			
In Freeform, boards can now be organised into folders.

Foundry




Weather
Weather gets a clearer and more detailed forecast interface, with reorganised information tiles and enhanced 10-day forecasts showing precipitation probability and amount, as well as wind speeds throughout the day.

				
					

				
			
In the Weather app, the tiles have been rearranged, and there are separate 10-day forecasts for precipitation and wind (circled in red).

Foundry




Shortcuts
Shortcuts gains a redesigned editor, more automation capabilities and one of macOS 27’s more ambitious AI features: the ability to turn natural-language instructions into working automations.

				
					

				
			
Shortcuts can start automatically when a specific event occurs.

Thomas Armbrüster




Parental Controls
Apple is expanding its family-safety tools with Safari’s Ask to Browse, improved Screen Time and Time Allowances, contact approvals and broader Communication Safety protections. The changes give parents more control over what children can access and who they can communicate with without completely locking down the Mac.
Accessibility, Shared Albums and Suggestions
macOS 27 also includes accessibility improvements, expanded Shared Albums and more contextual Suggestions throughout the operating system.
Game Porting Toolkit 4
Apple’s Game Porting Toolkit 4 arrives alongside macOS 27 and promises significant improvements for running and porting Windows games on Apple silicon Macs.
Early beta testing suggests substantial performance gains. On an M4 Pro MacBook Pro, GTA V reportedly increased from around 106fps to 176fps, while Red Dead Redemption 2 improved from roughly 60fps to 75fps.
The results suggest software compatibility, rather than raw Apple silicon performance, is increasingly the main obstacle to better Mac gaming. Improvements to Game Porting Toolkit could make Windows titles more practical to run and easier for developers to bring to macOS.


						

							


Design and Interface Changes in macOS 27

				
					

				
			
Apple




macOS 27 Golden Gate refines the Liquid Glass redesign introduced in macOS 26, with Apple focusing on readability, consistency and usability rather than another major visual overhaul.
Changes include:
Improved Liquid Glass: Stronger contrast, better readability and more consistent refraction effects across windows, menus and controls.
Customisable transparency: Users can adjust the Liquid Glass effect in System Settings, from a clearer appearance to a more heavily tinted look.
Cleaner Finder and toolbars: Finder sidebars are more clearly defined, toolbars are more consistent, and edge-to-edge sidebars replace some of the floating elements introduced in macOS 26.
More consistent windows: Window corners, controls and active-window highlighting have been standardised to make the interface feel more coherent.
Updated icons and menus: Menu-bar and app icons gain sharper outlines, improved contrast and more depth, while unnecessary menu icons have been reduced.
Smoother window management: Mission Control and Spaces animations have been refined, and active windows should be easier to distinguish.
New wallpapers and screensavers: Golden Gate-themed backgrounds include animated daytime and nighttime views of the bridge.
Swipe to refresh: Supported Mac apps gain a swipe-down-to-refresh gesture.
Improved iPhone Mirroring: iPhone Mirroring adds Control Center access, resizable app windows and support for DRM-protected video.

				
					

				
			
Foundry



							


Performance improvements and system changes in macOS 27
Apple says macOS 27 focuses on speed, efficiency and everyday usability, with improvements across apps, networking, displays and system tasks. Most of these changes do not require Apple Intelligence.
Changes include:
Faster overall performance: Apps should launch more quickly, while an optimised CPU scheduler improves system responsiveness.
Faster Spotlight and setup: Spotlight indexing and new user-account creation are quicker.
Faster file transfers and networking: AirDrop and network file browsing are faster, while Ethernet status can appear in the menu bar.
Thunderbolt and Bluetooth improvements: RDMA over Thunderbolt has been improved, alongside more efficient Bluetooth power management.
Faster Safari: The Safari Start Page loads more quickly, with broader browser performance improvements.
Better external-display support: New high-resolution and high-refresh-rate modes include 5K at 120Hz, alongside improved display-position persistence, HDR support for the macOS interface and 5K Mac mirroring.
Apple Intelligence powered changes:
AI-powered file naming – requires Apple Intelligence: macOS can suggest filenames and folder names based on their contents, including in Pages, Numbers, TextEdit and Finder.
Systemwide proofreading – requires Apple Intelligence: Apple Intelligence provides automatic proofreading and improved spelling and grammar suggestions throughout macOS.
Apple Intelligence privacy: Apple says AI processing happens on-device where possible, with Private Cloud Compute used for more demanding tasks. Data processed in the cloud is not stored or made accessible to Apple.


						

							


macOS 27 Compatible Macs 

				
					

				
			
The MacBook Neo and other Macs in Apple’s current lineup will all be compatible with macOS 27.

Foundry




Apple confirmed that macOS 27 Golden Gate is compatible with:
MacBook Neo (A18 Pro, 2026)
MacBook Air (Apple silicon, 2020 and later)
MacBook Pro (Apple silicon, 2020 and later)
iMac (Apple silicon, 2021 and later)
Mac mini (Apple silicon, 2020 and later)
Mac Studio (2022 and later)
Mac Pro (Apple silicon, 2023 and later)
All supported Macs can run Apple Intelligence, although some of the most advanced Siri AI features require an M3 or later Mac with at least 12GB of unified memory.
What about Intel Macs?
macOS 27 marks another major step in Apple’s transition away from Intel. macOS 26 Tahoe was the final version to support Intel Macs, and Apple is now encouraging developers to remove Intel code from their apps and focus on Apple silicon.
macOS 27 will also be the final version to support Rosetta, Apple’s translation technology for running Intel-only apps on Apple silicon Macs. Those apps will continue to work in macOS 27, but will stop working in macOS 28 unless developers release Apple silicon-native versions.
To help users prepare, macOS 27 includes an Intel-app checker in System Settings that lists Intel-based apps used during the past year. If you still rely on any essential Intel-only software, now is a good time to look for updates or alternatives before upgrading to macOS 28.
What happens to DVD support?
macOS 27 also begins the phase-out of Apple’s native DVD support. Apple has removed the DVDPlayback framework from the macOS 27 SDK and says it will disappear completely in a future version of macOS.
Golden Gate may still include the DVD Player app, but it is likely to be the last macOS release with Apple’s built-in DVD playback support. Users who still watch DVDs on a Mac will increasingly need to rely on third-party software such as VLC.


						

							





 FAQ 


1.
When will macOS 27 Golden Gate be released?
Apple hasn’t confirmed exactly when macOS 27 will be available to install, but it usually launches to the general public in September, or at the latest October. 
Once macOS 27 launches Apple will likely continue beta development to test new features that weren’t available at launch. 





2.
Should I install the macOS 27 beta?
Whether you should install the macOS 27 beta depends on your needs, technical expertise, and tolerance for bugs and instability. Beta software can introduce crashes, data loss, app compatibility problems, excessive battery drain, reduced performance, and other unexpected issues.
For most users, the recommendation is simple: don’t install it. If you’re eager to try the new features download the Public Beta – but avoid installing it on your primary Mac.
Developers are a different case. The Developer Beta is available now through Apple’s Developer Program, allowing app creators to test their software against new APIs, frameworks, and system features before the public release. If you’re not a developer, think carefully before installing the Developer Beta, as it is typically less stable and more prone to bugs than later beta releases.
Regardless of which beta you choose, make sure you have a complete backup of your Mac before upgrading.





3.
Which Macs can run macOS 27?
All M-series Macs will get macOS 27, and the MacBook Neo. 
Certain Siri AI features – most powerful on-device model, expressive voices and advanced dictation – will only be available for M3 Macs and newer.





4.
Should Intel Mac owners upgrade now?
Intel Mac owners should upgrade to Apple Silicon as soon as possible. The transition away from Intel hardware has reached a critical turning point, with software support rapidly vanishing and a new generation of affordable entry-level hardware making the switch more accessible than ever.
Apple has confirmed that macOS 27 will not support any Intel-based Macs. While a small number of Intel models may receive security patches for older versions of macOS until September 2028, they are already excluded from modern flagship features.
Those with Intel Macs also miss out on many features, including Apple Intelligence.





5.
Will macOS 27 support Rosetta and Intel apps?
macOS 27 will still run Intel-only Mac apps through Rosetta 2. However, macOS 27 will be the final version of macOS to support Rosetta 2 as a general-purpose translation technology for running Intel-based Mac apps on Apple silicon.
Rosetta has acted as a transition layer since Apple introduced its own Mac chips in 2020, translating x86_64 Intel instructions so older software can run on Apple silicon. After macOS 27, most Intel-only Mac apps will no longer work unless developers release Apple silicon-native versions, although Apple will retain limited Rosetta functionality for some older, unmaintained games.
Apple is already preparing users for the change. Since macOS 26.4, Macs can display warnings when launching apps that rely on Rosetta, encouraging users to update to Apple silicon-native versions before general Rosetta support ends.
In macOS 28, most Intel-only apps will no longer run unless developers update them for Apple silicon.





6.
When is macOS usually updated?
Here is a history of release dates for macOS:
macOS 26 Tahoe: September 15, 2025
macOS 15 Sequoia: September 16, 2024
macOS 14 Sonoma: September 26, 2023
macOS 13 Ventura: October 25, 2022
macOS 12 Monterey: October 25, 2021
macOS 11 Big Sur: November 19, 2020
macOS 10.15 Catalina: October 7, 2019
macOS 10.14 Mojave: September 24, 2018
macOS 10.13 High Sierra: September 25, 2017
macOS 10.12 Sierra: September 20, 2016

title: Every new Apple product coming in 2026 & 2027
content:
Macworld





It’s been a huge year for Apple, with a wave of new products arriving during the first nine months of 2026, including the MacBook Neo and iPhone 17e in March, then the new Mac mini and Mac Studio in August, and now the iPhone 18 Pro, 18 Pro Max and iPhone Duo, plus the Apple Watch Series 12, Ultra 4 and new AirPods 5 at Apple’s September 9 “Surprise and Shine” event.
There is plenty more on Apple’s roadmap, from new iPads and smart-home products to Apple’s first touchscreen MacBook Pro and smart glasses, all of which could arrive later in 2026 or early 2027.
Alongside the new hardware, Apple is preparing the public release of iOS 27, macOS 27 and its other next-generation operating systems, bringing the major Siri AI overhaul first previewed at WWDC in June. 
Here’s everything Apple has launched in 2026 so far – and what we expect to come next.
What else to expect from Apple in 2026
Biggest launch still to come: The first touchscreen MacBook Pro
Biggest software upgrades: iOS 27, macOS 27, major Siri/Apple Intelligence upgrade and deeper system-wide AI integration
Apple’s roadmap: At a glance
As of September 1, 2026, Apple’s roadmap has come under the direction of CEO John Ternus. Former CEO Tim Cook has moved into the executive chairman role. The shift from an operations-focused leader to one with deep hardware engineering roots could signal a more product-driven approach – and a renewed emphasis on standout hardware. Ternus took over as CEO just as Apple is preparing a major Siri overhaul, alongside potential launches including its first touchscreen MacBook.


ProductExpected releaseKey rumoursShould you wait?

iPad miniFall 2026Larger OLED screenYes
iPadFall 2026Apple Intelligence supportYes
MacBook Pro with TouchscreenLate 2026-early 2027Touch screenYes
Apple Smart GlassesPreview in late 2026 possibleCameras, audio, Siri/Visual IntelligenceYes
iPhone 18/iPhone Air 2Spring 2027iPhone 18 could merge with iPhone AirYes
iPhone 18eSpring 2027Possible Dynamic IslandNo

 






Every New Apple Product Launched in 2026… so far
Here is what Apple has already announced in 2026:
iPhone Duo: Apple’s first foldable iPhone: iPhone Duo Guide.
iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max: A20 Pro chip, upgraded vapor-chamber cooling, camera improvements: iPhone 18 Pro & Max Guide.
Apple Watch Series 12 & Ultra 4: Faster chips, Apple’s latest health-sensing features: Apple Watch Series 12 & Ultra 4.
AirPods 5: Stronger open-ear Active Noise Cancellation and longer battery life: AirPods 5.
Mac mini M6 and M5 Pro: Faster storage, upgraded connectivity, and a strong focus on AI performance: New Mac mini 2026 guide.
Mac Studio M5 Max and M5 Ultra: Faster AI and graphics performance, increased memory bandwidth: New Mac Studio 2026 guide.
AirPods Max 2: Improved audio and the H2 chip. Find out more here: AirPods Max 2 guide.
MacBook Neo: Apple’s brand new, low-cost Mac laptop. Find out more here: MacBook Neo guide.
MacBook Air M5: Now with the M5 chip. Read about the 2026 MacBook Air here: MacBook Air M5 guide.
MacBook Pro M5 Pro & M5 Max: A significant upgrade over the M4 series. Read: MacBook Pro M5 Pro & Max guide.
Studio Display: Finally gets Thunderbolt 5 and a better webcam. 
Studio Display XDR: With mini-LED technology and ProMotion up to 120Hz.
iPhone 17e: The new, entry-level, iPhone replaces the iPhone 16e. Read more here: iPhone 17e guide.
iPad Air M4: The iPad Air now has an M4 chip. Read more here: iPad Air M4 guide.
AirTag 2: Four years on Apple updated the AirTag, read our review here: AirTag 2nd gen review.
And… RIP Mac Pro: Apple has confirmed that it is discontinuing its tower workstation.  
Read on to find out what new products to expect at Apple’s next event and throughout 2026.


						

							







Every New Apple Product Launching in 2026
In the sections below we’ve split the upcoming new products into categories including Mac, iPad, iPhone, Apple Watch, Home, AirPods, and some new product categories.
Software updates coming in 2026
Apple Intelligence, Siri and AI
iOS 27 and macOS 27 Golden Gate, will introduce a massive overhaul to Siri and expanded Apple Intelligence capabilities.
iOS 27 is coming to compatible iPhones on September 14. Siri AI will launch in public beta later in 2026.
The All-New Siri AI
The most significant update is the transformation of Siri into Siri AI, a conversational assistant powered by Apple Intelligence. 
Key Siri AI features coming later in 2026 include:
Onscreen Awareness: Siri will understand and interact with what is displayed on your screen. For example, if a friend texts you an address, you can ask Siri to save it to a contact without leaving the app.
Dedicated Siri App: A new standalone app will allow you to revisit previous conversations, pin important chats, and sync history across all Apple devices via iCloud.
App Actions: Siri will be able to perform tasks within apps using natural language, such as editing a recently sent message or adding a song to a specific playlist.
Visual Intelligence: On iPhone, a new Siri mode in the Camera app will allow users to point their phone at objects to ask questions or perform actions based on what they see. On Mac, users can select onscreen content to ask Siri questions about images or documents.
Voice Customization: Users can personalize Siri with more natural voices and adjust the pace and expressiveness of the speech. This feature requires a M3 Mac with 12GB RAM or newer, or iPhone 17 Pro or iPhone Air and newer. 
Apple Intelligence Across Apps
Beyond Siri, Apple Intelligence is being integrated system-wide to automate tasks and enhance productivity. Apple Intelligence will play a larger role across the iPhone, iPad, Mac, smart home devices, and future product categories.
Major updates include:
Safari Productivity: The browser will automatically group tabs into topics, monitor pages for changes (like price drops) with a “Notify Me” feature, and even build custom extensions based on natural-language descriptions.
Smarter Photo Editing: New tools include Spatial Reframing to improve composition after a photo is taken, an Extend tool to fill in missing areas when straightening horizons, and an upgraded Clean Up tool for removing distractions.
Writing Tools and Communication: Mail and Messages will gain smarter replies that mimic a user’s writing style . System-wide Writing Tools will generate text from scratch, rewrite drafts, and adapt tone to match specific contacts.
Image Playground: This tool has been revamped with better language models to create more natural-looking photorealistic images. It also allows users to create custom wallpapers on iOS 27.
Intelligent Automation: The Shortcuts app will feature a “Describe a Shortcut” ability, allowing users to create complex automations simply by explaining what they want in plain English.


						

							


What new iPads are coming in 2026/2027 

				
					

				
			
Screenshot

Foundry




Don’t expect major redesigns for the iPads this year. Instead, Apple is likely to focus on faster chips and other internal upgrades. That said, both the iPad and iPad mini are due for an update – particularly the entry-level iPad, which currently lacks support for Apple Intelligence. Here’s what we expect Apple to announce:
iPad mini
Late 2026 update possible
The current iPad mini (A17 Pro) was released in October 2024, and Apple’s update cycle for this model is generally infrequent. Based on current reports and analysis, the next significant update to the iPad mini is not expected until late 2026, with some speculation pointing toward 2027.
One rumored upgrade for the 2026 iPad mini is the transition to an OLED display, which could reduce manufacturing costs and improve battery life. There is also the possibility of a slightly larger screen, with a move from the current 8.3- to 8.7-inches suggested. There is also speculation that a future foldable Apple device could potentially replace the iPad mini line entirely, though this remains uncertain. 
Internal code leaks suggest the future iPad mini could be upgraded to an A19 Pro chip, which would provide a significant performance boost over the current A17 Pro. An A18 Pro chip upgrade is also possible. Read our round up of iPad mini rumors.
iPad 
Late 2026 update possible
When the standard iPad was updated in March 11, 2025, the biggest disappointment was that it featured a A16 chip and therefore didn’t support Apple Intelligence. Apple looks set to rectify that in 2026 with an upgrade to the A18 or A19 chip, with the latter offering 50% better performance. The release timeline for an iPad with an A18 or A19 chip is anticipated before the end of 2026, in fact, Apple code suggests the company may be planning an update sooner-rather-than-later.
Read more about the 2026 iPad in our rumor round up. 
Should you buy now or wait? 
With the iPad prices increasing in June 2026, you may want to hold off buying one now. If you are going to pay more at least get the most up-to-date model, or buy from Apple’s Refurbished Store to get a bargain. Read Should I buy an iPad now or wait?


						

							


Which new Macs are coming in 2026/2027?
2026 is expected to be a significant year for the Mac, with Apple’s first touchscreen Mac rumored as part of a MacBook Pro redesign. March 3 saw the launch of the M5 MacBook Air and M5 Pro/M5 Max MacBook Pro and March 4 saw Apple introduce a new entry-level laptop – the $599 MacBook Neo.
The long expected Mac Studio and Mac mini updates came in August 2026 and go on sale September 22, although some high-memory Mac Studio configurations won’t arrive until later. These Macs have become popular for running AI models locally; however, global RAM shortages – driven by AI companies purchasing large amounts of memory for data centres – have been having a knock-on effect on availability during 2026 and these RAM shortages have also had an effect on prices, with Mac prices increasing by $300 to $500 in June and in the case of the Mac mini, by a further $100 with the 2026 lannch. 
One Mac that won’t be getting an update is the long-neglected Mac Pro. Apple has confirmed that the Mac Pro will be discontinued in favor of the Mac Studio.
Touchscreen MacBook Pro
Possible late 2026 introduction

				
					

				
			
Foundry




There are rumors that the MacBook Pro will get a redesign including notch-free OLED touchscreen, potential 5G connectivity and a thinner body. At one point it was expected that this new MacBook Pro would feature M6 Pro and Max chips, but the latest indications are that Apple will use M5 Pro and M5 Max chips instead in an effort to keep the project on schedule. 
Read the rumors about the M6 MacBook Pro with a touch screen.
iMac
Unlikely 2026 update
The current M4 iMac was released in October 2024, so an M5 update might seem timely and could be released alongside other potential M5 Mac updates.
The current iMac design was introduced in 2021 and is not expected to change soon. It is still considered fresh, and its components are not outdated. However, there are calls for Apple to introduce a larger screened iMac, something that has been missed since Apple discontinued the 27-inch model. Many feel that the 24-inch screen is too small. Read about the larger iMac rumors.
Should you buy now or wait? 
With the prices of Macs increasing in June due to the global RAM shortages you may want to hold off buying one now. If you are going to pay more at least get the most up-to-date model, or buy from Apple’s Refurbished Store to get a bargain. Read the following for more guidance:
Should you buy the MacBook Pro now or wait? 
Should you buy the MacBook Air now or wait?
Should you buy a Mac mini now or wait?
Should you buy a Mac Studio now or wait?


						

							


AirPod updates coming in 2026/2027
According to a brief update in Mark Gurman’s Power On newsletter for Bloomberg in August, Apple is aiming to launch camera-equipped AirPods.
The new earbuds are expected to resemble the upcoming AirPods Pro 3, although it’s not yet clear whether they will also include a heart rate sensor.
The cameras are said to include both visible-light and infrared sensors, but they reportedly won’t be designed for taking photos or recording video, as their placement and image quality would make them unsuitable for those tasks. Instead, the cameras are expected to enable AI-powered features, such as hand gesture recognition, adapting audio based on the surrounding environment, and detecting whether someone is speaking directly to you or simply talking nearby.


						

							


Apple Home updates coming in 2026/2027

				
					

				
			
Mahmoud Itani / Foundry




Apple is expected to significantly expand its smart home ecosystem in 2026 and 2027 with new devices beyond its traditional Apple TV and HomePods.
Rumored products include a smart home hub that combines HomePod functionality with a touchscreen, an updated HomePod mini 2 and next-generation Apple TV are also expected.
This strategic push could help Apple catch up with competitors like Amazon and Google in the smart home market.
Apple’s push into the smart home market will be heavily reliant on a significantly improved Siri, which is coming with iOS 27 and macOS 27.
New and updated products are said to include: 
HomePod mini 2
Fall 2026 introduction

				
					

				
			
Foundry




A new HomePod mini is said to be on the way with a faster processor that can take advantage of the new Siri AI. 
HomePod 3
Fall 2026 introduction
A new HomePod with an updated chip is also expected. 
Apple TV
Fall 2026 update
The current Apple TV isn’t compatible with Siri so an update is needed. Apple TV leaks indicate a rumoured Apple TV is on Apple’s roadmap and that the update will bring Apple Intelligence to the set top box.
New Smart Hub 
Possible 2026 introduction
Multiple reports have suggested Apple will launch a smart home hub. Apple is said to be working on a number of HomeHub related products including a device said to mount a camera on a robot arm that can follow you around! 
New Smart Display
Possible 2026 introduction
Also rumored is an iPad-like smart display that allows you to control your home devices via HomeOS software. This may come with both a speaker base and a wall mount.
HomePod Touch
Possible 2026 introduction
A new HomePod smart speaker with a screen is said to be coming. Read more here: New HomePod rumors.


						

							


What new iPhones are coming in 2027?

				
					

				
			There are new iPhones coming.
Foundry




Based on current industry analysis and supply chain information, Apple has some significant changes planned for the iPhone in 2027, with an 20th anniversary iPhone rumored as well as the iPhone 18, 18e and iPhone Air 2.
iPhone 18 & iPhone 18e
Spring 2027 launch expected
Reports suggest that Apple could delay the iPhone 18 and release that handset alongside the iPhone 18e in the spring of 2027.
iPhone Air 2
The iPhone Air could also be getting an update. But there are rumors that it will actually merge with the iPhone 18. See our iPhone Air 2 rumors.
Should you buy now or wait? 
With the iPhone 18 launch not expected until the spring, now is a good time to buy an iPhone 17. Read: When is the best time to buy an iPhone.
However, prices have already risen across the board, so it is no longer possible to beat the price hikes unless you find a refurbished iPhone.


						

							


Upcoming Vision devices, AR and spatial computing
Apple Smart Glasses 
Possible 2026 introduction, 2027 launch
Unlike the bulky Vision Pro headset, the upcoming smart glasses from Apple are expected to follow a form factor similar to the Ray-Ban Meta glasses. This will be Apple’s first product built specifically for “Visual Intelligence.” It will likely handle tasks such as live translations, music playback, phone calls, and turn-by-turn directions. Apple could provide a first glimpse or “preview” of the glasses by the end of 2026. 
Vision Pro
Possible 2027 update
Prior to 2026, Apple’s spatial computing strategy has focused on the high-end market, but reports indicate a more affordable version of the headset is in development. Apple has reportedly paused work on a successor to the high-end Vision Pro and will instead release a cheaper Vision Pro. 


						

							





What Apple launched in 2025
Here’s a quick look at what Apple released in 2025:
February 2025: iPhone 16E – the replacement for the iPhone SE and iPhone 14 brought Apple Intelligence support to the entry-level iPhone.
March 2025: iPad Air M3 and A16 iPad launched on March 4 and MacBook Air M4 and M4 Max Mac Studio on March 5.
September 2025: Apple introduced four new iPhones: iPhone 17, 17 Pro, 17 Pro Mac, and the iPhone Air. We also saw the new AirPods Pro 3 and three new Apple Watches: the Series 11, Ultra 3 and SE 3.
October 2025: Apple announced a new M5 processor and released the M5 MacBook Pro, M5 iPad Pro, and a update to the Vision Pro, featuring the new chip.

What Apple launched in 2024

What Apple launched in 2023
Apple hit the ground running in 2023 and closed the year with the Vision Pro, although it didn’t arrive until 2024:

title: Apple Reference Image is a new way to authenticate iPhone photography
content:
Apple Reference Image gives iPhone 18 Pro owners verifiable evidence of what the camera captured, offering a new defense against convincing AI-generated and edited images.

Apple Reference Image
The opt-in feature uses a new sensor in the Main camera that can sign every pixel it sees. Taking a photo in Reference mode captures signed sensor data that Private Cloud Compute turns into an unalterable reference image.
The Photos app displays that reference beside the main photo like a digital negative, allowing viewers to compare the two and determine whether edits were made. Apple's official release says the feature is designed for photojournalists, photographers, and everyday viewers.
Apple Reference Image first appeared in beta code in August. Apple has now confirmed that APIs in iOS 27, iPadOS 27, and macOS 27 will let third-party apps display reference images.
